Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 1b - taxable income before the standard/itemized deduction
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 1b = Form 1040 line 11b (AGI) minus line 1a, where line 1a = Form 1040 line 14 (total deductions) minus Schedule 1-A line 37 (the senior deduction). Algebraically line 1b = AGI - (totalDeductions - seniorDeduction) = taxable income + seniorDeduction: it restores the Schedule 1-A line 37 senior deduction (not allowed for the AMT) while leaving the line-38 tips/overtime/car-loan deductions (allowed for the AMT) in place. Computed directly from AGI so it can go negative ("if less than zero, enter as a negative amount") rather than reusing the floored /taxableIncome.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2a - taxes add-back
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 2a: if filing Schedule A, the taxes from Schedule A line 7 (scheduleA:/scheduleALine7TotalTaxes, line 5e SALT + line 6 other taxes — line 6 IS modelled, as the filer-entered writable /writableScheduleALine6OtherTaxes); otherwise the Form 1040 line 12e standard deduction (/standardOrItemizedDeductions, which equals the standard deduction when not itemizing) MINUS any net qualified disaster loss increase. This is the dominant AMT preference for this dictionary's population - the standard deduction and SALT are both disallowed for the AMT. EXCEPTION (2025 i4684): the AMT adjustment for the standard deduction is "made retroactively inapplicable to net qualified disaster losses" - the increase in the standard deduction attributable to a net qualified disaster loss (form4684:/netQualifiedDisasterLoss) is NOT added back, so it is subtracted here. On the form this is "enter zero on Form 6251, line 2a ... include the amount of your standard deduction (before it is increased by any net qualified disaster loss)"; modeled equivalently as add-back = base standard deduction (= increased standard deduction - net disaster loss). Byte-identical additive: net disaster loss is Complete-0 on every return without a qualified-disaster attestation.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2g, the municipal-fund leg - the IRC 57(a)(5)(B) exempt-interest-dividend share
Fact.Description:
The second of Form 6251 line 2g's two legs = the Form 1099-DIV box 13 total (dividendReports:/specifiedPrivateActivityBondInterestDividends). IRC 57(a)(5)(B) treats an exempt-interest dividend as interest on a specified private activity bond "to the extent of its proportionate share of the interest on such bonds received by the company paying such dividend" - a municipal bond FUND, whose shareholder holds no bond directly and therefore has nothing in Form 1099-INT box 9 at all. The two legs are DISJOINT populations reaching one printed line, which is why this fact ADDS to /amtLine2gPrivateActivityBondInterest rather than replacing it.
BOX 13, NOT BOX 12, and the distinction is the whole of the design. dividendReports exports both totals: /exemptInterestDividends is box 12, the entire exempt-interest dividend (the quantity Form 1040 line 2a is about), and /specifiedPrivateActivityBondInterestDividends is box 13, the private-activity SUBSET of it. Only the subset is a preference. Reading box 12 here would over-state AMTI for every fund holding any non-private-activity municipal bond, which is nearly all of them.
THE SHARE IS ALREADY NET OF EXPENSES AND THIS FACT DOES NOT RE-ALLOCATE IT. The instructions say more than the statute does: the dividends are treated as such interest "to the extent the dividends are attributable to interest on the bonds received by the company, minus an allocable share of the expenses paid or incurred by the company in earning the interest" (2025 Instructions for Form 6251, Line 2g). That allocation is the fund's, made before the payer prints box 13, and the same passage sends the filer to box 13 for the result - so this fact TRANSCRIBES and computes no proportion of its own. It could not compute one: no fund-level interest or expense figure has an intake anywhere in this dictionary, and inventing a second definition of a number the payer already reports is the double-intake shape income:/iraDistributions' contract refuses.
NO CONTAINMENT BOUND IS IMPOSED HERE, deliberately. Box 13 is a portion of box 12 on the printed form, but the intake declares only a Min $0 floor on each - a Limit may hold a literal and nothing else, and no Form 1099-DIV instruction set is vendored to state the arithmetic. Clamping the input here would silently repair a data-entry error, which is the failure the intake chose against.
UNROUNDED, NON-NEGATIVE, AND COMPLETE-SAFE WITHOUT A GUARD OF ITS OWN. The aggregate is unrounded against its own module's idiom precisely so this leg can join a line-2 summand; Form 6251 rounds once at line 4, as line 1b and line 2a already do. The amount is a share of interest received so no floor can bind, and the per-report writable carries a Min $0 anyway. The aggregate is itself an IsComplete/Switch over /dividendReports and resolves Complete $0 both for a return with no dividend reports and for a report that leaves box 13 unanswered - so a bare read adds NO Incomplete surface to /amtiBeforeMfsAddback, and a second wrapper here would be noise rather than safety.
WHAT THIS LEG STILL DOES NOT COVER, disclosed rather than left to inference. A filer filing Form 8814 must also include on line 2g the preference-item part of that form's line 1b tax-exempt interest (2025 Instructions for Form 6251, Line 2g). Form 8814 is not modelled anywhere in this dictionary, so no return can enter that amount and the omission is unreachable-by-input rather than silently wrong. Direction if that ever changes: the omission LOWERS AMTI, the World-#1-adverse side, and the Form 8814 unit owns it. "that ever changes" happened, and the owning unit is this one. Form 8814 IS now modelled (dictionary/ty2025/form8814.xml, the IRC 1(g)(7) election with a line 1b intake, /form8814Children/*/writableChildTaxExemptInterest), so "unreachable-by-input" no longer holds. The guard moved from unreachability to a refusal: form8814:/knockoutForm8814ChildTaxExemptInterest knocks the return out whenever any elected child's line 1b is nonzero, so no return ever COMPUTES with this line 2g term omitted — the omission stays disclosed, and the population that would owe it is turned away instead of silently under-taxed. The direction note stands. That knockout narrows when a successor lands the line 2g term here (which needs a PAB-portion intake, because line 1b mixes preference and non-preference interest) and the EIC Worksheet 1 line 2 term. LINE 2g NOW HAS THREE LEGS, so "the second of Form 6251 line 2g's two legs" and "the two legs are DISJOINT" above name two of three; this fact is still the second of them and its own content is unchanged. That successor is this change, and both owed terms landed together. The PAB-portion intake exists (form8814:/form8814Children/*/writableChildPrivateActivityBondInterest, per child) and its aggregate form8814:/form8814PrivateActivityBondInterest is now the THIRD summand of /amtLine2gPrivateActivityBondInterest below; the EIC Worksheet 1 line 2 term landed as form8814:/form8814TotalTaxExemptInterest inside eitc:/eitcInvestmentIncome. form8814:/knockoutForm8814ChildTaxExemptInterest was therefore DELETED, not narrowed - a nonzero line 1b now computes instead of refusing. The gap this paragraph opened by disclosing is CLOSED: the Form 8814 clause of i6251's Line 2g is covered. What survives of the direction note is smaller and is stated on the new facts: an unanswered PAB-portion split resolves $0, which still LOWERS AMTI, the World-#1-adverse side, and is the same accepted posture as the box-13 leg's own unanswered case.
ONE ADJACENT GAP IN ANOTHER MODULE, named only so a reader does not attribute it to this line: Form 1040 line 2a (interest:/taxExemptInterest) sums Form 1099-INT box 8 alone, so a pure fund holder's box-12 exempt-interest dividends do not reach it. That understates a reported-but-untaxed line rather than AMTI, and it is dividendReports/interest business, not form6251's.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2g - interest from specified private activity bonds (all three legs)
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 2g = the sum of three legs: Form 1099-INT box 9 across every interest report; the municipal-fund leg /amtLine2gExemptInterestDividendShare (Form 1099-DIV box 13); and the elected-child leg form8814:/form8814PrivateActivityBondInterest (the section 57(a)(5) preference portion of Form 8814 line 1b). IRC 57(a)(5)(A) makes this a preference item: "Interest on specified private activity bonds reduced by any deduction (not allowable in computing the regular tax) which would have been allowable if such interest were includible in gross income". The interest itself is excluded from gross income by section 103 - 57(a)(5)(C)(i) defines a specified private activity bond as one "issued after August 7, 1986, and the interest on which is not includible in gross income under section 103" - so this line is the AMT clawing back income the regular tax never saw. Box 9 is the payer's own identification of the amount ("Enter interest of $10 or more from specified private activity bonds ... See section 57(a)(5) for more details"), so no bond-level analysis is done or needed here.
THE 57(a)(5)(A) REDUCTION IS ZERO, and that is a modelled fact rather than an omission: the deduction it describes is one disallowed for the regular tax that WOULD have been allowed had the interest been taxable - an expense allocable to tax-exempt income, section 265. No such deduction has an intake anywhere in this dictionary, so no return can enter one and the reduction cannot be understated. Direction if that ever changes: a reduction LOWERS the preference, so a zero here is the World-#1-safe side.
THE EXEMPT-INTEREST-DIVIDEND LEG: a pure fund holder has no box 9, so interest:/flowKnockoutHasBonds does not refuse them, and /amtLine2gExemptInterestDividendShare (the dividendReports box-12/box-13 intake) is what keeps their line 2g from resolving zero. COMPLETE-SAFE, and the guard is load-bearing rather than decorative. This fact is a summand of /amtiBeforeMfsAddback, which reaches AMTI, /amtBaseOverExemption, the Form 6251 filing requirement, and the /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference exposure gate. An Incomplete here would propagate into all of them, so the IsComplete guard on /interestReports supplies a Complete 0 for any partial-computation scenario whose interest collection never initialises; the CollectionSum itself already yields 0 for an EMPTY collection and for reports that leave box 9 unanswered (interest:/interestReports/*/specifiedPrivateActivityBondInterest is itself the complete-safe alias over the writable). The fund leg needs no guard of its own for the same reason, stated on that fact: the box-13 aggregate it reads is already an IsComplete/Switch over /dividendReports. Every pre-existing scenario is therefore still byte-identical - no committed scenario answers box 13 any more than it answers box 9. UNROUNDED: this is a line-2 summand, and Form 6251 rounds once at line 4 (/alternativeMinimumTaxableIncome), matching the treatment of line 1b and line 2a. All three summands are unrounded for that reason, so no intermediate rounding is introduced by the addition.
NON-NEGATIVE by construction - interest received, less a reduction that section 57(a)(5)(A) caps at that same interest, plus a share of interest received - and no floor is declared because none can bind: box 9 and box 13 are both received amounts and the reduction is zero.
THE BOX-9 POPULATION: interest:/flowKnockoutHasBonds refuses a box 9 not covered by its own box 8 (a box-8/box-9 consistency gate) and boxes 10-13. IRC 56(b)(1)(B)(ii) makes box-9 interest count as investment income for the AMT's section 163(d) computation, which /amtLine2cInvestmentInterestDelta (Form 6251 line 2c) computes; a box 9 covered by its own box 8 does not refuse, so this line runs on that filer's submittable return. No committed scenario answers box 9 or box 13, so this module stays byte-identical on the corpus.
THE THIRD LEG, form8814:/form8814PrivateActivityBondInterest, is the section 57(a)(5) preference PORTION of an elected child's Form 8814 line 1b, which IRC 1(g)(7)(B)(iii) makes an item of tax preference "of such parent (and not of such child)"; i6251's Line 2g text carries the matching instruction, qualified - include "any tax-exempt interest income from line 1b of that form that is a preference item" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, page 4). It is a disjoint population from the other two: the box-9 filer holds the bond, the box-13 filer holds a fund, and this parent holds neither - the bond is the child's. So it ADDS, exactly as the fund leg does, and a parent in all three populations prints their sum.
ONLY THE PORTION REACHES THIS LINE. The WHOLE of Form 8814 line 1b is a different quantity with a different consumer - EIC Worksheet 1 line 2, through form8814:/form8814TotalTaxExemptInterest - and the two must not be crossed: the whole of line 1b here would OVER-state AMTI for any child holding ordinary municipal bonds.
THE DISCLOSED RESIDUAL THE THIRD LEG BRINGS, of the same species and direction as the box-13 one: the per-child portion is an optional writable and an unanswered one resolves $0, so an unanswered split leaves this line under-stated, the World-#1-adverse side. It is argued and bounded on the form8814 facts themselves.
COMPLETE-SAFETY AND BYTE-IDENTITY. The form8814 dependency is itself an IsComplete Switch over form8814:/form8814Children defaulting to $0 - the same construction the fund leg uses - so this Add gains no Incomplete surface, and a return that never opens the Form 8814 election adds exactly $0. No committed scenario references /form8814Children at all, so the corpus stays byte-identical.

Fact.Name: AMT Form 4952 line 3 - total investment interest expense, refigured for the AMT
Fact.Description:
Line 3 of the SECOND, AMT Form 4952 that the Form 6251 line-2c procedure calls for = AMT line 1 + AMT line 2. i6251 Step 1 leaves line 1 alone except for a widening that is $0 here (see below), and Step 2 replaces line 2 with the AMT attestation: "Enter your AMT disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 on line 2. Complete line 3."
THE ONLY TERM THAT DIVERGES FROM THE REGULAR TWIN IS LINE 2, and the divergence is real law rather than bookkeeping: a filer whose 2024 return carried private activity bond interest had a LARGER allowed AMT deduction in 2024 (IRC 56(b)(1)(B)(ii) makes that interest investment income for the AMT's section 163(d) pass) and therefore a SMALLER AMT disallowed carryforward into 2025. form4952:/amtInvestmentInterestCarryforwardIn is that attestation, and when it is unanswered it falls back to the REGULAR line 2 rather than to $0 - the "no 2024 AMT adjustment" reading. That fallback is what keeps this fact equal to its regular twin for the whole unanswered population, and hence keeps line 2c at $0 for them rather than manufacturing an addback out of nothing.
STEP 1'S WIDENING IS $0 ON EVERY RETURN THIS GRAPH CAN FILE, and it is a residue rather than a condition. Step 1 says to include on AMT line 1 "any interest that would have been deductible if tax-exempt interest on private activity bonds were includible in gross income" - interest expense the regular tax disallows under section 265 because it funded tax-exempt holdings. No intake for such an expense exists anywhere in this dictionary, so no return can enter one. Direction if that changes: it would ENLARGE the AMT deduction and make line 2c more negative, so a zero here is the World-#1-safe side.
INCOMPLETE UNTIL LINE 1 IS ANSWERED, exactly as its regular twin form4952:/totalInvestmentInterestExpense is, and deliberately not guarded. That Incomplete is the gate itself: /amtForm4952Line8Deduction reads this fact only inside an IsComplete(line 1) branch, so it never escapes. A complete-safe $0 here would be a WORSE shape, not a safer one - it would silently claim a filer with no Form 4952 has an AMT line 3 of zero rather than none, and it would move the gate into a place where a later reader cannot see it.

Fact.Name: AMT Form 4952 line 6 - section 163(d) net investment income, refigured for the AMT
Fact.Description:
Line 6 of the AMT Form 4952 = max($0, AMT line 4h minus line 5), where AMT line 4h is the regular line 4h WIDENED by Form 6251 line 2g. i6251 Step 3: "Include on line 4a any tax-exempt interest income from private activity bonds that must be included on Form 6251, line 2g." The statute behind it is IRC 56(b)(1)(B)(ii), which treats interest on a specified private activity bond "(and any amount treated as interest on a specified private activity bond under section 57(a)(5)(B))" as includible in gross income for purposes of applying section 163(d) - so the widening covers BOTH of line 2g's legs, the directly-held bond and the municipal-fund share, which is why this fact reads the whole /amtLine2gPrivateActivityBondInterest rather than its box-9 arm.
"BOTH of line 2g's legs" is now ALL THREE of them, and the substance of this paragraph is UNCHANGED - only the count word. The new third leg (form8814:/form8814PrivateActivityBondInterest, the elected child's section 57(a)(5) preference portion of Form 8814 line 1b) is squarely inside 56(b)(1)(B)(ii) on either reading: IRC 1(g)(7)(B)(iii) makes the child's 57(a)(5) preference the PARENT's preference of the SAME species it was in the child's hands, so whether the child held the bond directly (the 56(b)(1)(B)(ii) main clause) or through a fund (its "(and any amount treated as interest ... under section 57(a)(5)(B))" parenthetical), the amount is one 56(b)(1)(B)(ii) already covers. This fact still reads the WHOLE /amtLine2gPrivateActivityBondInterest and needs no logic change.
IT STARTS FROM THE UNFLOORED 4h, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF form4952's SEPARATE 4h FACT. The shipping line 6 (form4952:/section163dNetInvestmentIncome) is Round(max($0, 4h minus line 5)) and therefore DESTROYS the sign of (4h minus line 5): for a return whose investment expenses exceed its investment income the shipping line 6 is $0 and the shortfall is unrecoverable from it. Writing this fact as "the regular line 6 plus line 2g" would hand back line 2g in full wherever the truth is strictly less, OVER-stating AMT line 6, hence AMT line 8, hence making line 2c MORE negative, hence UNDER-stating AMTI. So it reads form4952:/section163dInvestmentIncome (line 4h, unfloored and unrounded, built for exactly this consumer) and applies its OWN floor and round.
LINE 5 IS THE REGULAR AMOUNT ON BOTH PASSES. form4952:/investmentExpenses is read as it stands; the AMT-only line-5 augmentation Step 3 permits has no intake in this dictionary and is disclosed as this change's one residue in the block header above.
IT ADDS NO INCOMPLETE SURFACE, unlike the line-3 twin, and that is the exact claim rather than "complete on every return" - which would be the overstatement the line 4h fact itself warns against. All three terms (line 4h, line 2g, line 5) are complete-safe, so this needs no guard and resolves $0 for a return with no investment income. But it INHERITS PLACEHOLDER from a Placeholder term, as form4952:/section163dInvestmentIncome does. That Placeholder cannot reach AMTI: /amtForm4952Line8Deduction gates on Form 4952 line 1 before reading this at all, and the same capture measures line 8 and line 2c Complete on all 938.

Fact.Name: AMT Form 4952 line 8 - investment interest expense deduction, refigured for the AMT
Fact.Description:
Line 8 of the AMT Form 4952 = the smaller of AMT line 3 and AMT line 6, on the same "Enter the smaller of line 3 or line 6" rule the regular pass uses.
THE GATE LIVES HERE, mirroring form4952:/investmentInterestExpenseDeduction's own shape exactly. i6251's precondition is "If you filled out Form 4952 ... for your regular tax, you will need to fill out a second Form 4952 for the AMT", so a return that never answered Form 4952 line 1 has no second pass to run and this line is $0 - not Incomplete, and not a min over an Incomplete line 3. Putting the IsComplete/Switch here rather than on line 2c keeps the two line 8s structurally identical, which is what makes their difference exactly $0 for the whole no-Form-4952 population instead of merely numerically $0.
THE FLOOR IS THE REGULAR PASS'S FLOOR AND NO OTHER. Line 6 is already floored at $0 by its own fact, and line 3 is non-negative (line 1 and both line 2s carry Min $0 limits), so the min cannot go below zero and no additional GreaterOf is declared.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2c - investment interest expense, the AMT-versus-regular-tax difference
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 2c = REGULAR Form 4952 line 8 minus AMT Form 4952 line 8.
THE SIGN IS THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REVERSE OF THE INSTRUCTION'S SURFACE READING. Step 4 says "Enter on Form 6251, line 2c, the difference between line 8 of your AMT Form 4952 and line 8 of your regular tax Form 4952. If your AMT expense is greater, enter the difference as a negative amount." Read literally the first clause is AMT minus regular, which is ALREADY positive when the AMT deduction is the larger one - so the second clause is not a special case, it is what fixes the convention: THE STORED VALUE IS REGULAR MINUS AMT. "The difference" in the first clause is a magnitude, not a signed subtraction. The same conclusion follows from the arithmetic of line 4, where 2c is a summand: a LARGER AMT deduction must LOWER AMTI. A build storing AMT minus regular would have this line backwards by twice the delta.
SIGNED, AND NOT FLOORED. The form prints line 2c without parentheses, unlike lines 2b and 2f, but a "difference between regular tax and AMT" is signed by construction and both directions occur: a smaller AMT carry-in gives an ADDBACK, and the line-2g widening of AMT investment income can give a SUBTRACTION. No rounding at this node beyond the rounding both line 8s already carry; Form 6251 rounds once at line 4.
THE PAIRING WITH LINE 2g IS NOT A CANCELLATION, and the boundary pair exists to stop that reading. Where the AMT line-6 cap does not bind, line 2c exactly offsets the line-2g addback and AMTI lands on the no-bonds figure - the full-offset case above resolves AMTI = AGI to the cent. Building line 2g without line 2c would over-state AMTI for the first filer; building 2c without 2g would understate it for the second.
A FILER WHO DID NOT ITEMIZE ENTERS NOTHING. The instructions say so in terms: "If you didn't itemize deductions and you had investment interest expense, don't enter an amount on Form 6251, line 2c, unless you reported investment interest expense on Schedule E". The regular Form 4952 line 8 reaches only Schedule A line 9 in this dictionary, so a filer taking the standard deduction takes no investment interest deduction on either pass and the difference is $0. The gate is taxCalculations /wantsStandardDeduction, the same test line 2a (/amtiTaxesAddback) uses to choose between the standard deduction and Schedule A taxes: it is true unless Schedule A is claimed AND either exceeds the standard deduction or is elected on Schedule A line 18, so a filer who answered that they have itemized deductions but whose return takes the larger standard deduction also enters nothing here. The Schedule E exception is not reachable here: no fact routes any part of Form 4952 line 8 to Schedule E, so no return this dictionary represents reported investment interest expense there.
COMPLETE ON EVERY RETURN, with no guard of its own beyond that gate, because both operands are: form4952:/investmentInterestExpenseDeduction and /amtForm4952Line8Deduction each carry the same IsComplete(Form 4952 line 1) switch and each resolve Complete $0 for the population that never filed a Form 4952. That is load-bearing rather than tidy - this fact is a summand of /amtiBeforeMfsAddback, which reaches AMTI, /amtBaseOverExemption, the Form 6251 filing requirement and the /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference exposure gate, so an Incomplete here would propagate into all of them.
VALUE-MOVING BUT BYTE-IDENTICAL ON THE CORPUS, provable rather than observed. AMT line 3 equals regular line 3 unless the AMT carry-in writable is answered, and AMT line 6 equals regular line 6 unless line 2g is nonzero; no committed scenario does either, so both minima pick the same operand and this line is $0 on every one of them.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2e - the regular-tax net operating loss deduction, added BACK to AMTI
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 2e = 0 minus income:/schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction, the net operating loss deduction Schedule 1 line 8a carries, stated as a positive amount. The printed line is "Net operating loss deduction from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8a. Enter as a positive amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 1), printed WITHOUT parentheses, so it is an addition to AMTI: the AMT disallows the regular-tax NOL deduction outright and allows only its own ATNOLD on line 2f instead.
READ FROM LINE 8a ITSELF, AS PRINTED. Schedule 1 line 8a is a preprinted-parentheses field, so income:/schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction is NEGATIVE whenever the deduction is positive, and line 2e negates it once. Line 8a has two sources: the form172 carry-in inventory (the 80-percent-limited deduction, form172 /form172Schedule1NolDeductionAdjustment), which governs whenever it holds a loss, and the older single figure income:/writableNetOperatingLossDeduction. Line 2e once read that older figure directly and so printed $0 for a filer whose deduction came from the inventory, understating AMTI by the whole deduction. Reading line 8a picks up whichever source line 8a used. Line 8a carries nothing but this deduction.
COMPLETE WHENEVER LINE 8a IS: $0 on a return with no NOL deduction, and Incomplete while line 8a waits for the carry-in inventory (a positive older figure with no inventory item).
WHAT THE ADD-BACK DOES TO AMTI, measured on the node-test pair. The deduction reaches the AMT through /amtiLine1b, which is AGI minus line 1a: a return answering a 24,000 NOL has AGI 24,000 lower, so line 1b is 24,000 lower. Line 2e restores exactly that 24,000, so AMTI is EQUAL on the two members of the pair while regular-tax AGI differs by the full deduction. That equality is the correctness claim, not an absence of effect: without this fact the same return would reach AMTI 96,000 instead of 120,000, and with the sign inverted it would reach 72,000.
WHY THIS MATTERS: without this fact, AMTI would be understated by the full deduction for every filer who answers the NOL intake, in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, which is a World-1 error rather than a conservative omission.
SCOPE, PLAINLY: this is line 2e ONLY. Line 2f (the ATNOLD) is /amtLine2fAlternativeTaxNolDeduction, computed against /amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold's 90-percent cap; the pair is the AMT's whole treatment of net operating losses.
COMPLETE ON A RETURN THAT ANSWERS NOTHING. This fact is a summand of /amtiBeforeMfsAddback, which carries no guard of its own and reaches AMTI, /amtBaseOverExemption, /tentativeMinimumTax, the Form 6251 filing requirement and /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference. Line 8a is itself $0 when neither NOL source is answered.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (line 8a is never above $0). No rounding at this node - Form 6251 rounds once at line 4.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 lines 1 through 3, tentative - AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD (the section 56(d)(1) 90-percent cap base)
Fact.Description:
The section 56(d)(1)(A)(i)(II) cap base: "90 percent of alternative minimum taxable income determined without regard to such deduction and the deduction under section 199". The 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 give the operative procedure under the Line 2f heading: "To figure the ATNOLD limitation, you must first figure your AMTI without regard to the ATNOLD. To do this, first figure a tentative amount for line 2d by treating line 2f as if it were zero. Next, figure a tentative total of lines 1 through 3 using the tentative line 2d amount and treating line 2f as if it were zero. This is your AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD. Your ATNOLD is limited to 90% of the result" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, page 3, the LEFT column of a two-column extraction).
IT IS A HOIST, NOT A PARALLEL SHADOW CHAIN, AND THAT IS THIS FACT'S WHOLE DESIGN CLAIM. A "without regard to X" re-evaluation reads like it needs a duplicate of the lines 1 through 3 chain with one term suppressed, and this engine has no re-evaluate-with-one-term-zeroed operator. It needs neither. The two substitutions the instruction prescribes are line 2f and the tentative line 2d, and BOTH are top-level terms of the same combine - so zeroing them is just the combine without those summands, and the 2f-free partial sum is a SUB-EXPRESSION of the shipping total rather than a copy of it. This fact is therefore the primitive and /amtiBeforeMfsAddback reads it, not the reverse. That direction is forced rather than chosen: deriving the base by subtracting line 2f back out of the shipping combine would make the cap base a function of the deduction it caps, a circularity.
HOW IT RELATES TO /amtiBeforeMfsAddback. Line 2f (/amtLine2fAlternativeTaxNolDeduction) joins /amtiBeforeMfsAddback and NEVER this fact, so the two diverge by exactly the ATNOLD whenever the ATNOL pool is answered and are equal otherwise; node-test form6251/amt-line2f-atnold-capped-at-90-percent pins the divergence (base 120,000 against a post-deduction 12,000).
THE BASE IS LINES 1 THROUGH 3, NOT LINE 4, AND THAT IS A DECIDED QUESTION WITH A RECORDED TENSION. Form 6251 line 4 is this combine PLUS the married-filing-separately add-back and, for a REMIC residual holder, floored at Schedule E line 38 column (c). The printed procedure says "a tentative total of lines 1 through 3" and then equates that total to "your AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD", so neither the add-back nor the floor belongs to the base and this fact sits below both. The competing reading is not frivolous: IRC 55(d)(2)'s flush sentence makes the add-back an increase to AMTI itself ("In the case of a taxpayer described in paragraph (1)(C), alternative minimum taxable income shall be increased by the lesser of (i) 25 percent of the excess of alternative minimum taxable income (determined without regard to this sentence) over the minimum amount of such income (as so determined) for which the exemption amount under paragraph (1)(C) is zero, or (ii) such exemption amount (determined without regard to this paragraph)", 26 U.S.C. 55, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section55&num=0&edition=2024), and section 860E does the same for the excess-inclusion floor. Three reasons converge on the printed reading. (1) The instruction is the operative procedure for this very limitation and says lines 1 through 3 literally. (2) The direction is conservative: a SMALLER base gives a smaller 90-percent cap, a smaller allowed ATNOLD and therefore a HIGHER AMTI, which is the World-#1 side. (3) The add-back is computed FROM this combine, so folding it into the base would put the cap base downstream of a quantity that is itself downstream of the ATNOLD once line 2f exists; the statute's own "(determined without regard to this sentence)" parenthetical breaks the add-back's self-reference but not that loop, while "lines 1 through 3" breaks it cleanly.
THE DIVERGENCE WITNESSES ARE THE MFS AND REMIC CASES, and they are the only place this fact is testable at all. Against /amtiBeforeMfsAddback it differs only by line 2f; against Form 6251 line 4 it differs wherever the add-back or the floor moves. On the i6251 printed illustration the base is 920,350 against line 4 of 925,350.
BOTH PRONGS OF THE LIMITATION SHARE THIS BASE (/amtAtnoldFirstProng and /amtAtnoldSecondProng). The instructions' special rule for qualified disaster / Gulf Opportunity Zone / recovery assistance losses and 172(b)(1)(H) carrybacks takes "90% of AMTI for the tax year (figured without regard to the ATNOLD)" in its prong 1b and "100% of AMTI for the tax year (figured without regard to the ATNOLD) reduced by the amount determined under (1)" in its prong 2b (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, page 3, the RIGHT column of the same two-column extraction). One quantity, both prongs.
THE TENTATIVE LINE 2d IS NOT SEPARATELY FIGURED. The instruction figures this base with a tentative line 2d (line 2d refigured with line 2f treated as zero). This combine reads the shipping /amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment, so it equals the instruction's figure wherever line 2d does not itself turn on line 2f; a separate tentative-2d twin is the named open refinement.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED. It inherits /amtiLine1b, which is computed from AGI precisely so it can go negative, and /amtLine2cInvestmentInterestDelta, which is a signed delta. NO ROUNDING HERE, and that is deferred rather than settled: Form 6251 rounds once at line 4, so the combine is unrounded, and whether the 90-percent product is taken on the unrounded base is line 2f's question. A negative base yields a negative 90-percent cap, which drives the ATNOLD to zero under line 2f's printed min(ATNOLD, limitation).
THE COMBINE: /amtiLine1b plus every Form 6251 line 2 and line 3 adjustment except line 2f - lines 2a through 2e, 2g through 2t and line 3. /amtiBeforeMfsAddback is this fact plus line 2f.

Fact.Name: Alternative tax net operating loss available from earlier years (Form 6251 line 2f input)
Fact.Description:
THE ATNOL POOL: the AMT-basis remainder of net operating losses from earlier years that is available to deduct this year — the "sum of the ATNOL carrybacks and carryforwards" the Form 6251 instructions name. Answered as a POSITIVE amount; the negative sign the printed line 2f carries is applied downstream by /amtLine2fAlternativeTaxNolDeduction, never here.
A CARRY-IN ATTESTATION. An ATNOL is by nature multi-year state and the graph holds none, so the available shape is an attested prior-year balance — exactly the shape /writableNonrecapturedSection1231Loss (form4797) and /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear (scheduleD) already use. Refusing the population instead would have been strictly worse: a filer with an ATNOL is representable today (income:/writableNetOperatingLossDeduction is answerable) and a zero line 2f OVER-states their AMTI.
IT IS NOT THE SAME QUANTITY AS THE REGULAR-TAX INTAKE, which is the confusion this pool is most likely to be filled in from. income:/writableNetOperatingLossDeduction is the CURRENT-YEAR regular-tax deduction under section 172; this is the AMT-BASIS remainder of EARLIER-year losses, recomputed under AMT rules. The two are different numbers on any return where an AMT adjustment touched the loss year, and nothing in this dictionary derives one from the other.
PAIR: the intake-side name is the settled ...FromPriorTaxYear shape; its emit-side twin is /alternativeTaxNolCarryoverToNextYear, the incoming pool less the amount this year's ATNOLD used. Neither half computes a NEW current-year AMT net operating loss; that boundary is stated on the emit fact.
SIGN: Min 0 declared rather than implied. The pool is an amount of loss AVAILABLE, and the instructions describe it as a sum of carrybacks and carryforwards; a negative pool has no printed meaning. UNANSWERED IS UNANSWERED — the complete-safe default lives on the line-2f fact, so a return that never had an ATNOL resolves line 2f Complete 0 without answering anything. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The ATNOLD limitation — 90% of AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD
Fact.Description:
Section 56(d)(1)(A)(i)(II): 90 percent of alternative minimum taxable income figured without regard to the ATNOLD. The base is /amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold, the hoisted lines-1-through-3 combine that exists precisely so this percentage is NOT a function of the deduction it caps.
THE BASE IS FLOORED AT ZERO BEFORE THE PERCENTAGE, and that is a build decision rather than a printed one, so it is stated. A negative AMTI-without-regard would make 90% of it negative, and LesserOf(pool, a negative limitation) would then produce a NEGATIVE ATNOLD — i.e. line 2f would ADD to AMTI, turning a deduction into an addback. Nothing printed sanctions that. Flooring the base at 0 yields a 0 limitation, hence a 0 deduction, for a filer whose AMTI is already at or below zero — the conservative reading, and the one that keeps line 2f a deduction in every state.
THIS IS PRONG 1(b) OF A TWO-PRONG LIMITATION. The instructions carry a second allowance for ATNOLs attributable to qualified disaster, Gulf Opportunity Zone or recovery-assistance losses, or a 2008-or-2009 loss carried back more than 2 years under section 172(b)(1)(H): that share of the pool is capped not at 90 percent but at 100 percent of the same base reduced by prong 1. The share is the filer's /writableAlternativeTaxNolCarryoverExceptedFromNinetyPercentLimit, and the two prongs are /amtAtnoldFirstProng and /amtAtnoldSecondProng; line 2f is their sum. A filer who answers no excepted share takes prong 1 alone, which is exactly the 90-percent rule this fact states. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The part of the ATNOL pool the 90 percent limit does not reach (Form 6251 line 2f input)
Fact.Description: The part of /writableAlternativeTaxNolCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear, the ATNOL pool, that is attributable to qualified disaster losses, qualified Gulf Opportunity Zone losses, qualified recovery assistance losses, qualified disaster recovery assistance losses, or a 2008 or 2009 loss the filer elected to carry back more than 2 years under section 172(b)(1)(H). The instructions exempt that share from the 90 percent ATNOLD limit and give it a second allowance of up to 100 percent of AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD, reduced by the general allowance. Answered as a POSITIVE amount and as a PART of the pool, not in addition to it: /amtAtnoldExceptedPool caps it at the pool and floors it at $0, because the Min limit below is not enforced when the fact resolves. Unanswered means no part of the pool is excepted, so the general 90 percent rule governs the whole pool. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The excepted share of the ATNOL pool, floored and capped at the pool
Fact.Description: /writableAlternativeTaxNolCarryoverExceptedFromNinetyPercentLimit floored at $0 and capped at the floored pool /writableAlternativeTaxNolCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear, when both are answered; $0 when the excepted share is unanswered. The share is a part of the pool, so it can never exceed it, and a negative answer means nothing. This is item 2a of the instructions' two-prong limitation. Read only on the line 2f arm that requires the pool answered.

Fact.Name: The general share of the ATNOL pool, to which the 90 percent limit applies
Fact.Description: The floored ATNOL pool less /amtAtnoldExceptedPool: the carrybacks and carryforwards attributable to net operating losses other than the excepted ones, item 1a of the instructions' two-prong limitation. Never negative, because the excepted share is capped at the pool. Incomplete when the pool is unanswered, which is why line 2f reads it only on its answered-pool arm.

Fact.Name: ATNOLD limitation prong 1, the smaller of the general share and 90 percent of the base
Fact.Description: Item 1 of the instructions' ATNOLD limitation: the smaller of /amtAtnoldGeneralPool and /amtAtnoldLimitation (90 percent of AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD, the base floored at zero). With no excepted share answered this is the smaller of the whole pool and the 90 percent limitation, the rule line 2f applied before the second prong existed.

Fact.Name: ATNOLD limitation prong 2, the excepted share up to the base less prong 1
Fact.Description: Item 2 of the instructions' ATNOLD limitation: the smaller of /amtAtnoldExceptedPool and 100 percent of AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD reduced by /amtAtnoldFirstProng. The base is floored at zero exactly as /amtAtnoldLimitation floors it, and the reduced base is floored again so a zero base can never turn the second allowance into an addback. $0 whenever no excepted share is answered.

Fact.Name: The ATNOL pool remaining after this year's deduction, carried to next year
Fact.Description:
The AMT-basis net operating loss remaining to carry to next year: the incoming pool less the amount this year's ATNOLD actually used, floored at 0. This is the figure a filer would attest into NEXT year's /writableAlternativeTaxNolCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear, and it completes the pair whose other half is the prior-year intake.
THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT AND NEEDS NO NEW INTAKE, which is why this is buildable where three earlier readings said it was not. /amtLine2fAlternativeTaxNolDeduction IS the negated amount used — it is 0 minus the two ATNOLD prongs — so the remainder is simply pool PLUS line 2f. Nothing is estimated: when the limitation binds, the unused part carries; when it does not, the pool is exhausted and this is 0. The retired contract declared exactly these two dependencies and this is what they compose to.
WHAT IT DOES NOT INCLUDE, AND THIS IS THE BOUNDARY OF THE FILL: a NEW current-year AMT net operating loss. A fresh NOL is Form 172 arithmetic performed on an AMT basis, and this dictionary computes no current-year NOL on EITHER basis — income:/writableNetOperatingLoss Deduction is an attested deduction for a loss from an EARLIER year, not a computed loss. So this fact is the carryforward of the INCOMING pool and nothing more. DIRECTION, stated because it is not symmetric: for a filer who generated a new AMT loss this year, this figure is TOO LOW, and attesting it next year would under-deduct. TAXPAYER-ADVERSE. That is why the companion flag below exists rather than a silent number.
WHY IT IS STILL WORTH SHIPPING: for every filer whose current year produced no new loss — which is the overwhelming majority, and every filer whose return this graph can compute a positive taxable income for — the figure is EXACT, and today they get nothing at all. The alternative was leaving the pair permanently half-built.
Complete-safe: an unanswered pool carries nothing forward, so this resolves Complete $0 on every return that never had an ATNOL. NON-NEGATIVE by the GreaterOf — a pool smaller than the deduction cannot carry a negative remainder. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The ATNOL carryforward may omit a new current-year loss (disclosure flag)
Fact.Description:
True when the return shows a NEGATIVE total income, which is the signal that the filer may have generated a new net operating loss this year — and therefore that /alternativeTaxNolCarryoverToNextYear, which carries only the INCOMING pool's remainder, may be too low.
IT REPORTS, IT DOES NOT CORRECT. Nothing reads it to change a dollar. Its job is to stop a partial figure being mistaken for a complete one: a filer flagged here must figure any current-year AMT loss on Form 172 on an AMT basis and add it before attesting next year's pool. That is the same posture scheduleE:/scheduleELine42AttestationDiffersFromComputed takes — surface the disagreement, resolve nothing.
WHY NEGATIVE TOTAL INCOME IS THE INDICATOR, and why over-flagging is the right error. A current-year NOL needs business losses, and negative total income can arise without one, so this flag is BROADER than the population it warns about. That direction is deliberate: a false warning costs a filer a check they did not need, while a missed one costs them a deduction. /taxableIncome is useless as the indicator because it is FLOORED AT ZERO by the printed line-15 rule, so it cannot distinguish a break-even return from a heavily loss- making one; total income is not floored and can. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2f — the alternative tax net operating loss deduction (ATNOLD)
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 2f = the smaller of the ATNOL pool and the ATNOLD limitation, entered as a NEGATIVE amount. Complete-safe $0 when the pool is unanswered. The limitation has two prongs, so the amount subtracted is /amtAtnoldFirstProng (the general share capped at 90 percent of the base) plus /amtAtnoldSecondProng (the excepted share capped at the base less prong 1); each prong is already the smaller of its share and its cap, so their sum is the smaller of the pool and the whole limitation.
THE ORDER AND THE SIGN ARE BOTH PRINTED, not inferred: "Enter on line 2f the smaller of the ATNOLD or the ATNOLD limitation. Enter it as a negative amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, page 3). So the limitation CAPS the pool rather than replacing it, and the entry is the negation of that minimum. The attested ATNOL pool is declared non-negative; floor it at $0 on this resolution path so an invalid negative seed cannot turn a deduction into a positive AMTI addback. The printed line itself carries parentheses (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 1), which is the second witness to the sign.
WHERE IT IS ADDED, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING THE RETIRED CONTRACT SAID NO TEST COULD ENFORCE: it joins /amtiBeforeMfsAddback and NEVER /amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold. The hoisted base must stay free of the deduction whose 90-percent cap it computes, or the cap becomes a function of the deduction it caps. Until this change the two facts were equal on every return, so nothing could fail if a build got it wrong; THEY DIVERGE whenever the pool is answered, and the node test amt-line2f-atnold-capped-at-90-percent pins the divergence directly — base 120,000 against a post-deduction 12,000. The prose-only period is over.
A ZERO POOL AND AN UNANSWERED POOL AGREE HERE, deliberately: both give line 2f = 0. The distinction is preserved on the writable (Incomplete vs Complete 0) for anyone who needs it, but no printed consequence turns on it — a taxpayer with no earlier-year AMT loss and one who attests zero take the same line.
WHAT THIS LINE IS NOT: the regular-tax NOL deduction. That is line 2e (/amtLine2eNolDeductionAddback), which ADDS the section 172 deduction back as a positive amount. The pair is the AMT's whole treatment of net operating losses — disallow the regular deduction, allow a separately-computed AMT one — and a graph carrying only one of them is wrong in a direction the other was meant to offset. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: AMTI before the married-filing-separately add-back (line 1b + line 2a + line 2c + line 2e + line 2g + line 2f)
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 4 components in scope: line 1b + line 2a + line 2c + line 2e + line 2g. The remaining lines 2b-3 (tax refund, the modeled-zero preferences, and other adjustments) are 0 for this population by the World-#1 scope-out handling documented in the module header, so this is the AMTI before the MFS line-4 add-back.
THIS FACT ADDS LINE 2f TO THE HOISTED BASE. The five summands above are held by /amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold, the section 56(d)(1)(A)(i)(II) cap base - "AMTI figured without regard to the ATNOLD" - and this fact is that base plus /amtLine2fAlternativeTaxNolDeduction. Line 2f is added HERE and not to the hoisted base, so the base stays free of the deduction whose 90-percent cap it computes; the two facts diverge by exactly line 2f whenever the ATNOL pool is answered. The placement is restated on the hoisted fact's own Derived comment.
LINE 2e CANCELS ANOTHER TERM OF THIS SAME COMBINE. /amtLine2eNolDeductionAddback is the regular-tax net operating loss deduction entered back as a POSITIVE amount, and the deduction it adds back is the same one that already reduced /amtiLine1b through AGI - so on a return answering an NOL the two moves are equal and opposite and AMTI is unchanged, which is exactly what the AMT's disallowance of the regular-tax NOL means. It is complete-safe 0 on every committed scenario (none answers income:/writableNetOperatingLossDeduction), so this combine stays byte-identical.
LINE 2g is complete-safe 0 on every return with no Form 1099-INT box 9 amount and no Form 1099-DIV box 13 amount, so every pre-existing scenario is byte-identical. Both populations this line moves are filable: the box-13 fund holder is not refused, and the box-9 holder whose box 8 covers box 9 is not refused either (interest:/flowKnockoutHasBonds is a box-8/box-9 consistency gate) - see that fact's Description for which box-9 cells still are.
LINE 2c IS THE FIRST SIGNED SUMMAND HERE. Lines 1b, 2a and 2g are all non-negative; /amtLine2cInvestmentInterestDelta is regular Form 4952 line 8 minus the AMT twin and goes negative whenever the AMT deduction is the larger one, which is exactly what line 2g's own widening of AMT investment income causes. The two therefore travel together: a filer with private activity bond interest AND investment interest expense gets an addback from 2g and a partial or full offset from 2c, and neither term is correct without the other. Both are complete-safe 0 on every committed scenario, so this combine is byte-identical on the corpus.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 4 married-filing-separately add-back
Fact.Description:
For married filing separately with AMTI over $900,350, an additional amount is added to line 4 to reconstruct the exemption benefit: 25% of the excess over $900,350, capped at $68,500 (reached at $1,174,350). Zero for every other filing status and for MFS at or below $900,350.
BOTH ARMS OF THE LesserOf ARE WITNESSED. The $68,500 cap is the section 55(d) exemption amount itself, and a case in which it BINDS needs AMTI strictly above $1,174,350 — at exactly $1,174,350 the two operands are equal, so that point is a tie and proves nothing about which arm was selected. The three node tests that now pin it: form6251/amt-mfs-addback-published-example reproduces the instructions' own illustration ($920,350 becomes $925,350, the additional $5,000 being 25% of $20,000); form6251/amt-mfs-addback-cap-one-dollar-under sits one dollar under the printed $1,174,350 and takes the 25% arm at $68,499.75; and form6251/amt-mfs-addback-cap-binds sits at $1,300,000, where the uncapped figure would be $99,912.50 and the cap holds the add-back to $68,500 — a $31,412.50 divergence, which is what makes it a witness rather than a coincidence.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 4 - Alternative Minimum Taxable Income (AMTI)
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 4 = line 1b + line 2a (+ the MFS over-900,350 add-back), floored at any REMIC excess inclusion. The unmodeled preference lines are handled by the World-#1 scope-out design (module header): documented-zero where no intake exists, and a submission knockout where a Schedule C / Schedule E / prior-year-MTC intake could carry an unmodeled adjustment.
THE SECTION 860E FLOOR. A Schedule E Part IV column (c) excess inclusion "is also the smallest amount you are allowed to report as your alternative minimum taxable income (AMTI) on Form 6251, line 4"; operatively, "if the amount in column (c) is larger than your AMTI would otherwise be, enter the amount from column (c) on Form 6251, line 4."
WHY THE GUARD, AND WHY THIS SITE DOES NOT LOOK LIKE ITS SIBLING. The other floor site, taxCalculations:/taxableIncome, adds the excess inclusion as a bare third GreaterOf arm, which is safe there because line 15 already carries a <Dollar>0 arm that dominates a non-negative addend. AMTI HAS NO SUCH ARM AND IS SIGNED: /amtiLine1b is computed from AGI precisely so it can go negative ("if less than zero, enter as a negative amount"), so a bare GreaterOf(line 4, excess inclusion) would clamp a negative AMTI up to 0 on every return in the corpus — a value change on returns that have no REMIC at all. The Switch applies the floor ONLY when the excess inclusion is positive, which makes the no-REMIC case byte-identical by construction rather than by argument. THE FLOOR IS APPLIED AFTER THE MFS ADD-BACK, AND THAT ORDER IS PRINTED, not chosen. These instructions carry a section headed "Special Rule for Holders of a Residual Interest in a Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit (REMIC)" which states the floor in this form's own words — "the amount you enter on line 4 may not be less than the amount on Schedule E, line 38, column (c). If the amount in column (c) is larger than the amount you would otherwise enter on line 4, enter the amount from column (c) instead" — and then settles the ordering explicitly: "If your filing status is married filing separately, be sure to include the additional amount that must be added to line 4 (as explained above) BEFORE you compare line 4 with the amount on Schedule E, line 38, column (c)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, pages 2, 9). Add-back first, comparison second, which is precisely GreaterOf(Add(before, addback), column (c)).
THAT PASSAGE WAS MISSED ON A FIRST PASS and the miss is recorded because it shaped this landing. Reading only the SCHEDULE E instructions — the form column (c) is reported on — the order looks undecidable: that form says to enter column (c) on line 4, while this form's line-4 caption ("If married filing separately and line 4 is more than $900,350, see instructions") can be read as applying the add-back on top of the floored figure. The answer was in the instructions for the form the amount is APPLIED to, under a heading naming this exact population. An interim knockout that refused MFS returns was built on the undecidable reading and retired in the same landing once this passage was found.

Fact.Name: AMT exemption base amount (Form 6251 line 5 middle column)
Fact.Description: The 2025 AMT exemption before phaseout: $137,000 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; $68,500 married filing separately; $88,100 single or head of household.

Fact.Name: AMT exemption phaseout threshold (Exemption Worksheet line 3)
Fact.Description: The AMTI above which the AMT exemption phases out at 25%: $1,252,700 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; $626,350 for all other filing statuses (single, head of household, and married filing separately).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 5 - AMT exemption
Fact.Description: Exemption Worksheet: the base exemption reduced by 25% of AMTI (line 4) over the phaseout threshold, floored at 0. The floor automatically yields 0 at or above the complete phaseout point ($978,750 single/HoH, $1,800,700 MFJ/QSS, $900,350 MFS), matching the worksheet note.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 6 - AMTI over the exemption
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 6 = AMTI (line 4) minus the exemption (line 5), floored at 0. The base to which the 26%/28% tentative-minimum-tax rate applies.

Fact.Name: AMT 28% rate breakpoint (Form 6251 line 7)
Fact.Description: The AMT base above which the 28% rate replaces 26%: $239,100 for all filing statuses except married filing separately, where it is $119,550.

Fact.Name: AMT 28% bracket adjustment (Form 6251 line 7 subtraction)
Fact.Description: The amount subtracted when the 28% rate applies to the whole base (the 2% of the breakpoint that was taxed at 26% rather than 28%): $4,782 for all filing statuses except married filing separately, where it is $2,391. Equal to 2% of the breakpoint.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 Part III line 13 - AMT preferential-rate income, whichever worksheet applies
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 Part III line 13, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "Enter the amount from line 4 of the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Form 1040 or the amount from line 13 of the Schedule D Tax Worksheet in the Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040), whichever applies (as refigured for the AMT, if necessary)." THIS FACT IS LINE 13 ONLY. Line 15 is its own fact, /amtPart3PreferentialIncomeWithUnrecaptured, which this fact does not speak for.
"WHICHEVER APPLIES" IS THE SAME SELECTOR FORM 1040 LINE 16 USES: scheduleD /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet, the Schedule D Tax Worksheet's own entry test. On an SDTW return the amount is scheduleD /sdtwLine13 (the 0/15/20% share of the gain, i.e. total preferential income LESS the 25% and 28% shares); otherwise it is /qdcgLine4 (qualified dividends + net capital gain), exactly as before. Reading /qdcgLine4 on an SDTW return would not merely be unfaithful, it would silently re-zero the 25% slice: line 22 = smaller of line 12 or line 13 would then equal line 16, and line 36 = line 16 - line 22 would be 0 by construction (see the Part III block header).
"AS REFIGURED FOR THE AMT" IS A CLAIM THIS FACT OWNS, NOT ONE IT INHERITS. Both worksheet amounts are identical for the AMT and the regular tax on the modeled population: the graph's capital gains and qualified dividends carry no AMT basis, ISO or depreciation adjustment (line 2k and the Schedule D differences are documented zero, module header). The ONE place a difference could arise is depreciation on section 1250 property, since section 1250 property is by definition depreciable, and the argument for that leg lives on /amtPart3UnrecapturedGain below, which is the fact Schedule D line 19 actually reaches. form4797 admits an attested section 1250 disposition (/section1245Dispositions/*/isSection1250Property) and takes the filer's own line 26a additional-depreciation carry-in, and Schedule D line 19 has SEVEN legs - scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250GainLine13 adds the lines 1-9 block (whose lines 1-3 are a CollectionSum of form4797 /section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent), the partnership-interest sale, the Form 1099-DIV box 2b dividends leg, Form 2439, Schedule K-1, the Form 1099-R leg, and other dispositions.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 Part III line 14 - unrecaptured section 1250 gain (Schedule D line 19)
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 Part III line 14, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "Enter the amount from Schedule D (Form 1040), line 19 (as refigured for the AMT, if necessary)." That is scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250Gain, read unconditionally: the form does not condition line 14 on which worksheet was used, and a return with no Schedule D line 19 resolves it Complete at $0, which is exactly the "zero or blank" state the skip instruction above line 35 names.
THIS FACT EXISTS TO GIVE THE REFIGURING CLAIM A HOME rather than to add arithmetic. scheduleD /unrecapturedSection1250Gain is line 13 less line 17, floored at zero, and line 13 is an Add over SEVEN legs - the lines 1-9 capped block (/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine9, whose lines 1-3 are a CollectionSum of form4797 /section1245Dispositions/*/unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent, i.e. the FILER'S OWN section 1250 property, with its line 26a additional-depreciation carry-in), the partnership-interest sale, the Form 1099-DIV box 2b dividends leg, Form 2439, Schedule K-1, the Form 1099-R leg, and other dispositions. A filer's own depreciation history reaches this line.
WHY THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ANYWAY FOR THE PROPERTY THIS GRAPH IS MOST LIKELY TO SEE, and the statute is quoted rather than paraphrased. IRC 56(a)(1)(A)(i): "Except as provided in clause (ii), the depreciation deduction allowable under section 167 with respect to any tangible property placed in service after December 31, 1986, shall be determined under the alternative system of section 168(g). In the case of property placed in service after December 31, 1998, the preceding sentence shall not apply but clause (ii) shall continue to apply." And clause (ii), after prescribing the 150-percent declining balance method: "The preceding sentence shall not apply to any section 1250 property (as defined in section 1250(c)) (and the straight line method shall be used for such section 1250 property)." 26 U.S.C. 56, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section56&num=0&edition=2024 for clause (i), lines 66-82 for clause (ii) - the RIGHT column of a two-column extraction, reassembled before quoting, because a downward read interleaves it with the 1986-Act estate-and-trust transition note in the left column. So for section 1250 property placed in service AFTER 1998 the ADS sentence is switched off and the AMT method is straight line, which is also the regular-tax method for post-1986 realty: no AMT depreciation adjustment, no basis difference, nothing to refigure.
THE RESIDUAL, NAMED RATHER THAN SILENCED, and it is NOT discharged by this fact. Fact.Name: Form 6251 Part III line 15 - preferential income including the 25% slice
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 Part III line 15, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "If you did not complete a Schedule D Tax Worksheet for the regular tax or the AMT, enter the amount from line 13. Otherwise, add lines 13 and 14, and enter the smaller of that result or the amount from line 10 of the Schedule D Tax Worksheet (as refigured for the AMT, if necessary)." Encoded exactly as written: the same scheduleD /useScheduleDTaxWorksheet selector chooses the arm, and the SDTW arm is the SMALLER of (line 13 + line 14) and scheduleD /sdtwLine10.
WHY THE SMALLER-OF IS NOT DECORATION, AND EXACTLY WHEN IT BINDS. SDTW line 10 is the whole preferential income and SDTW line 13 is that same amount less the 25%/28% share (SDTW line 12 = smaller of SDTW line 9 or Schedule D lines 18 + 19). So, writing s9/s10/s12/s13 for the SDTW lines and sd18/sd19 for the Schedule D lines,
line 13 + line 14 > line 10 <=> (s10 - s12) + sd19 > s10 <=> sd19 > s12 = min(s9, sd18 + sd19)
and since sd18 is floored at zero, sd19 > sd18 + sd19 is impossible; the min can only be broken through on its s9 side. THE CAP THEREFORE BINDS IF AND ONLY IF Schedule D line 19 > SDTW line 9, and Schedule D line 18 IS NOT PART OF THE CONDITION AT ALL.
AN EARLIER FORM OF THIS PARAGRAPH SAID THE OPPOSITE - that a nonzero Schedule D line 18 is what makes the sum overshoot - and a nonzero line 18 in fact pushes the other way, by raising s11 = sd18 + sd19 and so making s12 = s9 (the binding branch) LESS likely, not more. The counter-example, which is the shortest disproof: sd18 = 30, sd19 = 40, s9 = 100, s6 = 100. Then s10 = 200, s11 = 70, s12 = min(100, 70) = 70, s13 = 130, and line 13 + line 14 = 170, which UNDERSHOOTS s10 = 200 by 30 even though line 18 is nonzero. Whenever s9 >= sd18 + sd19 with sd18 > 0 the sum undershoots by exactly sd18.
WHAT MAKES IT BIND IN PRACTICE is a Schedule D line 19 larger than the net capital gain it sits inside - a Form 1099-DIV box 2b amount offset by a current-year long-term loss, so that Schedule D line 15 (and with it SDTW line 9) shrinks while line 19 keeps the whole box 2b figure. The amt-part3-line15-cap-binds node test is exactly that return, WITH Schedule D line 18 AT ZERO so the corrected condition is the only thing doing the work: box 2a 100,000, box 2b 80,000, a 60,000 long-term loss, a 1,000 short-term gain. Schedule D line 19 = 80,000 against SDTW line 9 = 40,000, the cap bites by 40,000, and it is what stops line 36 taxing 80,000 at 25% when the regular tax's own SDTW line 39 allows only 27,950. Direction, as that test measures it: deleting the smaller-of moves 40,000 out of line 17 (26%) into line 36 (25%) and LOWERS the AMT by 400 - the cap removes an under-statement.
LINE 15 IS NEVER LESS THAN LINE 13, which is the property lines 16, 22 and 36 lean on: on the no-SDTW arm they are equal by construction, and on the SDTW arm line 13 + line 14 >= line 13 while /sdtwLine10 >= /sdtwLine13 (line 12 of that worksheet is non-negative), so the smaller of the two still dominates line 13. Line 36 = line 16 - line 22 is therefore non-negative without needing a floor the form does not print.
WHEN LINE 14 IS ZERO THIS FACT COLLAPSES TO LINE 13 ON BOTH ARMS, which is how the skip instruction above line 35 ("If line 14 is zero or blank, skip lines 35 through 37", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2) is honoured without a Switch: the no-SDTW arm is line 13 outright, and on the SDTW arm smaller(line 13 + 0, /sdtwLine10) = line 13 because line 13 never exceeds line 10. Line 16 then equals line 22, line 36 is 0 and line 37 is 0 - the skip, produced by the arithmetic.

Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Form 6251 Part III lines 35-36 - the amount taxed at 25%
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 Part III lines 35 and 36 in one fact, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "35. Add lines 17, 32, and 33" and "36. Subtract line 35 from line 12". An ADD then a SUBTRACT; there is no smaller-of and no floor anywhere in this group, and none is added here. Line 32 is not a separate fact in this module (it is inlined at /amtPart3TwentyRateAmount as line 23 + line 30), so it enters as its two terms: line 35 = line 17 + line 23 + line 30 + line 33.
WHAT LINE 36 ACTUALLY IS. Lines 23, 30 and 33 partition line 22 exactly - line 33 = line 22 - (line 23 + line 30) and that subtraction never goes negative, because line 23 <= line 22 and line 30 <= line 24 = line 22 - line 23 - so line 32 + line 33 = line 22 identically. Hence line 35 = line 17 + line 22 = (line 12 - line 16) + line 22 and
line 36 = line 12 - line 35 = line 16 - line 22
the difference between the preferential income WITH the unrecaptured slice (line 16) and WITHOUT it (line 22): the 25% slice, as much of it as the AMT base can hold. That identity is why line 36 needs no floor - line 15 is never less than line 13 (/amtPart3PreferentialIncomeWithUnrecaptured proves it), so line 16 is never less than line 22 - and it is also why this fact cannot be built while one fact serves both line 16 and line 22.
THE SKIP IS PRODUCED, NOT ENCODED. The instruction above line 35 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2) reads "If line 14 is zero or blank, skip lines 35 through 37 and go to line 38", and a skipped line contributes $0. No Switch implements it because the arithmetic already does: when line 14 is $0, line 15 collapses to line 13 on both of its arms, so line 16 = line 22 and this fact is $0 exactly. That is the whole modeled population today except returns carrying a Form 1099-DIV box 2b amount, and it is what keeps the conformance corpus byte-identical.
COMPLETE-SAFE, and by the same route: every operand is a Part III fact that resolves exactly when /amtBaseOverExemption does, so this fact adds no new completeness hole. UNROUNDED - the single Round of Part III is at /tentativeMinimumTax (line 40).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 Part III line 37 - tax at 25%
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 37, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 2, verbatim: "Multiply line 36 by 25% (0.25)".
