Fact.Name: Form 6251 Part III line 38 - AMT using maximum capital gains rates
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 38 = line 18 + line 31 + line 34 + line 37: the 26%/28% tax on the ordinary portion plus the 0%/15%/20% tax on the preferential slice plus the 25% tax on the unrecaptured-section-1250 slice. Compared against the full-rate line 39 at line 40 (/tentativeMinimumTax). Unrounded; the single Round is at line 40.
FILLING LINE 37 RAISES LINE 38, NEVER LOWERS IT: while line 13 read /qdcgLine4, the unrecaptured slice stayed INSIDE line 22 and was taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% by lines 23-34; line 37 moves that slice OUT of line 22 (line 13 is now the SDTW's line 13) and taxes it at 25% instead, so line 38 rises by (25% minus the rate the slice would otherwise draw) times the slice. The line-13/15/16/22 split is what makes line 36 nonzero at all, so there is no configuration in which line 37 is populated and line 38 is unaffected.
WORLD #1 IS SATISFIED BY THAT DIRECTION: filling line 37 removes an under-statement of the AMT for a filer with unrecaptured section 1250 gain. The lesser-of at line 40 still caps the result at the full-26%/28% line 39, and the cap still cannot be breached: every Part III rate (0%, 15%, 20%, 25%, and the 26%/28% of line 18 itself) is at or below the line-39 rate, so line 38 <= line 39 continues to hold with the fourth term present. A return with no unrecaptured section 1250 gain has line 37 = 0 and is byte-identical to the previous body.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 7 / Part III line 40 - tentative minimum tax (BEFORE the line-8 AMTFTC)
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 40 = the SMALLER of the Part III maximum-capital-gains-rate tax (line 38, /amtPart3TentativeTax) and the full-26%/28% tax on the whole AMT base (line 39, computed inline below - 26% of line 6 if at or below the breakpoint, otherwise 28% of line 6 minus the bracket adjustment). Line 8 (AMT foreign tax credit) is now MODELED as Schedule 3 line 1 (/amtForeignTaxCredit) and is subtracted at line 9 downstream (in /alternativeMinimumTax), NOT here: this fact is line 7 / line 40, the tentative minimum tax BEFORE the line-8 AMTFTC subtraction. THIS FACT IS NOT LINE 9 — line 9 is its own fact, /amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftc, and the Name above used to read "line 7 / line 9 / Part III line 40" as though the two were interchangeable. They are not: they differ by exactly the AMTFTC, and 2025 Form 8801 line 23 reads LINE 9. Anything reaching off-form for "the tentative minimum tax" must check which of the two it means. THE PREFERENTIAL-RATE REFINEMENT: a flat build would tax the FULL base at 26%/28% (an over-statement for returns with qualified dividends or net long-term capital gain); Part III taxes the preferential slice at 0%/15%/20% instead. Because every preferential rate is <= 26%/28%, line 38 <= line 39, so the lesser-of only moves the tentative minimum tax DOWN or leaves it equal - never up. For a return with NO preferential income line 38 = line 39 exactly, so the value is identical to a flat 26%/28% tax. THE 25% TERM (line 37) DOES NOT DISTURB THAT BOUND: 25% is also at or below the line-39 rate, so line 38 <= line 39 still holds with all four terms present. What the 25% term DOES change is the comparison against the previous body, and in the opposite direction - see /amtPart3TentativeTax, which owns that argument: restoring line 37 raises line 38 for a filer with unrecaptured section 1250 gain, correcting an under-statement rather than conceding an over-statement.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 8 - alternative minimum tax foreign tax credit (AMTFTC)
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 8 = Schedule 3 (Form 1040) line 1, the foreign tax credit. For the no-Form-1116 IRC 904(j) election the 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 (Line 8, "Figuring the AMTFTC") state the AMTFTC "is the same as the foreign tax credit on Schedule 3 (Form 1040), line 1", so line 8 is exact there. A return may also take its credit from Form 1116 (schedule3 /sched3Line1 reads form1116 /form1116Line35ForeignTaxCredit when the filer opened Form 1116 and the exception does not apply). Then the AMTFTC is figured on a separate AMT Form 1116, which is not built, and this line carries the regular credit instead; /knockoutAmtForeignTaxCreditNeedsAmtForm1116 refuses every such return where the difference can reach a dollar. Line 8 = Schedule 3 line 1 on every return that files. Subtracting this at line 9 (line 9 = line 7 - line 8) makes the foreign tax credit CANCEL between the tentative-minimum-tax term and the regular-tax term of the AMT: line 11 = line 9 - line 10 = (TMT - FTC) - (regular - FTC) = TMT - regular, because line 10 (/amtRegularTaxForComparison) already subtracts the SAME Schedule 3 line 1. Leaving line 8 at 0 (the prior behavior) left line 10's FTC subtraction uncancelled, so the AMT was OVERSTATED by exactly the foreign tax credit - overcharging a 904(j) FTC-electing filer who owes AMT by up to $600 (MFJ) / $300 . Complete-safe: Schedule 3 line 1 is complete-safe 0 whenever there is no FTC, so this resolves 0 on every non-FTC return (byte-identical to the prior line-8 = 0). No cycle: Schedule 3 line 1's line-level cap was deliberately repointed to Schedule 2 line 1a (NOT the AMT), so /sched3Line1 does not depend on the AMT - this reference is acyclic, the same direction line 10 already uses.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 9 - tentative minimum tax after the AMTFTC
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 9 = line 7 MINUS line 8: "Tentative minimum tax. Subtract line 8 from line 7" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 1). Line 7 is /tentativeMinimumTax and line 8 is /amtForeignTaxCredit, so this is exactly those two facts differenced.
WHY IT EXISTS AS ITS OWN FACT, when line 11 already computes the same difference inline. Line 9 has a SECOND consumer outside this form: 2025 Form 8801 line 23 is "Enter the amount from your 2025 Form 6251, line 9, or 2025 Schedule I (Form 1041), line 52" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8801.pdf, page 2). Until now the only place line 9 existed was inside /alternativeMinimumTax's single Subtract, which removes line 8 and line 10 from line 7 in one expression - line 9 was never materialised, so a Form 8801 build had no fact to read and the nearest-looking one, /tentativeMinimumTax, is line 7, NOT line 9. Reading line 7 there would overstate 8801 line 23 by exactly the foreign tax credit, which understates 8801 line 24 and therefore the minimum tax credit: taxpayer-ADVERSE, and the same error class as the AMT-FTC defect already corrected once in this module. This fact is the correct edge.
LINE 9 IS NOT FLOORED HERE. The printed line carries no "if zero or less, enter -0-" - that floor is at line 11 ("AMT. Subtract line 10 from line 9. If zero or less, enter -0-", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 1). So a return whose AMTFTC exceeds its tentative minimum tax has a NEGATIVE line 9, which line 11 floors afterwards. The credit limits that copy line 9 (Form 8834 line 5, Form 8911 line 8, Form 3800 line 14 and Form 8801 line 23) read /amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftcFloored instead, which floors it at zero. Flooring does not cut the minimum tax credit: an unfloored negative line 23 lifts Form 8801 line 24 above line 22, the regular tax left after the other credits, so the line 25 credit could exceed the tax it offsets. That fact's Description gives the reasons.
NOT ROUNDED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE - it keeps this fact ADDITIVE. /tentativeMinimumTax is already Round()ed and /amtForeignTaxCredit is a bare pass-through of schedule3 /sched3Line1 (itself unrounded, reading foreignTaxCredit /foreignTaxCreditAmount). This body is therefore structurally IDENTICAL to the corresponding slice of /alternativeMinimumTax's inline Subtract, so materialising it changes no existing value.
ITS CONSUMER IS FORM 6251 LINE 11 ITSELF, and wiring it there is why this fact is not an orphan. Line 11 is printed as "AMT. Subtract line 10 from LINE 9", so /alternativeMinimumTax was rebodied to read this fact minus /amtRegularTaxForComparison instead of differencing line 7, line 8 and line 10 in one expression. That is the form's own structure, not a gratuitous refactor, and it means every AMT scenario in the corpus now exercises line 9. The Form 8801 build becomes the SECOND consumer.
THE REBODY IS VALUE-IDENTICAL, and the reason is exact arithmetic rather than luck. This fact carries NO Round, so line 11 went from Round(GreaterOf(l7 - (l8 + l10), 0)) to Round(GreaterOf((l7 - l8) - l10, 0)) with no intermediate rounding introduced between the two subtractions - the engine differences exact quantities, so the two associations are the same number. HAD THIS FACT BEEN ROUNDED the rebody would NOT have been safe: it would have become Round(GreaterOf(Round(l7 - l8) - l10, 0)), a possible one-cent shift on every FTC-electing AMT return. The missing Round is load-bearing, not an oversight. Completeness is unchanged too: this fact is Complete exactly when line 7 and line 8 are, which is the same set the old one-expression body needed.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 9 floored at zero - the tentative minimum tax the credit limits read
Fact.Description:
The tentative minimum tax that four credit limits copy from Form 6251 line 9: Form 8834 line 5, Form 8911 line 8, Form 3800 line 14 and Form 8801 line 23 each say "Enter the amount from Form 6251, line 9". It is line 7 less the line 8 AMT foreign tax credit (/amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftc), floored at zero. One fact serves all four readers so they cannot drift apart.
WHICH AMOUNT. Line 7 less the AMT foreign tax credit, whether or not the filer owes AMT. For these credits the Code defines "tentative minimum tax" as the section 55(b)(1) amount (section 26(c)), and section 55(b)(1) reduces that amount by the AMT foreign tax credit. The unreduced line 7 has its own defined name, "pre-credit tentative minimum tax" (section 59(a)(2)), and none of the four limits uses it. Each limit's regular-tax side is already net of the foreign tax credit, so only the reduced figure lets the credit cancel. The Form 6251 instructions let a filer who owes no AMT leave line 8 blank. That is a shortcut for line 11, which is zero either way, and it is not followed here: line 8 and line 9 carry the credit, so the credit forms copy the statutory amount. With no Form 1116 (the no-Form-1116 election) the difference from the shortcut is at most the smaller of line 7 and the credit ($300, or $600 on a joint return), in the filer's favour. On a Form 1116 return line 8 is not yet the AMT foreign tax credit (no AMT Form 1116 is built), and /knockoutAmtForeignTaxCreditNeedsAmtForm1116 refuses the returns where that reaches a dollar.
THE FLOOR. The graph's line 9 goes below zero when the AMT foreign tax credit exceeds line 7, for example when alternative minimum taxable income is under the exemption. The statute states no floor for that case, so the floor is a position: a credit taken against the pre-credit tentative minimum tax cannot take a tax below zero, and a negative figure would lift each limit above the regular tax it caps (Form 8834 line 6, Form 8911 line 9 and Form 8801 line 24 would exceed the net regular tax on the line above them). The floor changes no AMT dollar (line 11 compares line 9 with line 10, which is itself never below zero) and no general business credit dollar (Form 3800 line 15 takes the greater of line 13, never below zero, and line 14). On Form 8801 it removes a line 25 credit larger than the tax it offsets, and the matching shortfall in the line 26 carryforward. Printed Form 6251 line 9 stays signed, as the form prints it.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 10 - regular tax for the AMT comparison
Fact.Description:
Form 6251 line 10 = Form 1040 line 16 (regular tax, refigured without Schedule J, MINUS any tax from Form 4972, which form1099RFrontier /form4972TaxTotal carries) plus Schedule 2 line 1z (the additions-to-tax subtotal, = the PTC repayment in scope) minus Schedule 3 line 1 (the foreign tax credit) and minus any NEGATIVE Form 8978 line 14, treated as a positive number, floored at 0. SUBTRACTING the foreign tax credit is required for World #1: it lowers the regular tax and therefore RAISES the AMT (the safe direction) on a return claiming the credit.
THE FORM 8978 SUBTRAHEND IS BUILT, and the earlier claim "no Form 8978 negative in scope" while both the printed line and the instruction name the amount. That claim was a Bucket-0 silent wrong answer in the ADVERSE direction: without the subtrahend line 10 is overstated by the absolute value of the negative Form 8978 line 14, line 11 (the AMT) is understated by the same number, and the filer is UNDER-charged. The two clauses about Form 4972 and Schedule J were stale in the same sentence - the body has subtracted /form4972TaxTotal and read /line16WithoutScheduleJ for some time - so the whole sentence is rewritten rather than patched.
IT READS THE RAW WRITABLE, NOT schedule3 /sched3Line6l, for two independent reasons. (1) QUANTITY. Line 10 wants the FULL negative line 14 as a positive number. /sched3Line6l is that amount CAPPED at Form 1040 line 18 by the "Negative Form 8978 Adjustment Worksheet - Schedule 3 (Line 6l)", whose step 2 is exactly the raw quantity this fact needs and which schedule3 holds as /sched3Line6lWorksheetLine2NegativeForm8978Amount. On a return where the cap binds, reading /sched3Line6l would under-subtract and re-open the same adverse error in miniature. (2) CYCLE. /sched3Line6l reads taxCalculations /totalTentativeTax (worksheet line 1, Form 1040 line 18), which carries Schedule 2 line 3, which carries /alternativeMinimumTax, which reads THIS fact. The raw intake has no such edge. form1116 /form1116Line20RegularTaxPlusSchedule2Line1z reads the same writable for the same two reasons; this fact is the second consumer of that shape.
THE GUARD IS ISCOMPLETE-FIRST AND DEFAULTS TO $0, and that is load-bearing rather than defensive. A bare Dependency on a schedule3 writable that almost no return answers would make line 10 - and therefore the AMT, Schedule 2 line 2 and total tax - INCOMPLETE on every return that files no Form 8978. The Switch resolves to $0 whenever the writable is unanswered, so line 10 is unchanged there to the cent. THE MINUEND IS THE WITHOUT-SCHEDULE-J LINE 16. A filer who used Schedule J to figure Form 1040 line 16 must refigure that tax, including any tax from Form 8814, without using Schedule J before completing Form 6251 line 10, and only for Form 6251, so this fact reads taxCalculations:/line16WithoutScheduleJ instead of line 16 itself; on every return that does not elect income averaging the two are the same number.

Fact.Name: Claims the prior-year minimum tax credit (Form 8801)
Fact.Description:
Whether the return claims a credit for prior-year minimum tax (Form 8801).
THE CREDIT IS GENUINELY MULTI-YEAR, which is why Form 8801 Part II (at the end of this module) computes it from THREE ATTESTED prior-year carry-INs rather than deriving them - an attestation posture, not an engine capability. It computes and reaches Schedule 3 line 6b.
ANSWERING TRUE DOES NOT BY ITSELF KNOCK OUT THE RETURN: the /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference arm reading this flag fires only on "this flag AND an intake whose AMT adjustment is unmodeled" (Schedule C, royalty, K-1, estate/trust K-1, farm rental, or a rental carrying an AMT depreciation intake). A claimant with none of those FILES, and the credit reduces the tax. A claimant with one of them is still refused, because Form 8801 line 23 reads this form's line 9 and an understated AMTI would buy an overstated credit - the arm's re-derived ground, on the knockout's own Description. This flag is ALSO Form 8801 line 21's own gate, which is what makes the zero credit faithful rather than conservative for a non-claimant. Optional - a return with no such claim never answers this (complete-safe).

Fact.Name: Claims the prior-year minimum tax credit (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: /writableClaimsPriorYearMinimumTaxCredit when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern) - every prior scenario resolves false and stays value-identical.

Fact.Name: Knockout: return carries an unmodeled AMT preference/adjustment
Fact.Description:
BLOCKS SUBMISSION when the return has an intake that could carry an AMT adjustment or preference this module does not model, so that AMTI (and therefore the AMT) is never silently under-stated (World #1). interpretation: owner ruling, see TAX-INTERPRETATIONS-FOR-EXPERT-REVIEW.md OT-02. Two triggers, both narrowed from an original blanket trigger - "any Schedule C income OR any Schedule E rental income" (in the AMT zone) - to fire only on a return that actually carries an AMT-adjustment-creating intake, since the blanket over-refused business/rental/SE returns whose depreciation is entirely straight-line (a residential rental building has NO AMT depreciation adjustment) or whose Schedule C net income carries no separately-intaked accelerated depreciation: (1) A FORM 8801 PRIOR-YEAR MINIMUM TAX CREDIT CLAIM BESIDE AN INTAKE WHOSE AMT ADJUSTMENT THIS DICTIONARY DOES NOT MODEL. Form 8801 Part II (at the end of this module) computes the credit and wires it to Schedule 3 line 6b, so this arm protects an exposure the credit creates.
THE EXPOSURE THIS ARM PROTECTS, and it is a NEW exposure this module created rather than an old one inherited: Form 8801 line 23 is this form's LINE 9, so an understated AMTI understates line 23, OVERSTATES line 24 (= line 22 - line 23) and hence OVERSTATES the credit line 25 allows. And the credit is only ever positive when line 22 exceeds line 23, i.e. when the regular tax exceeds the tentative minimum tax - which is exactly the zone where line 11 (the AMT itself) is zero on BOTH the modeled and the true AMTI. So for the MTC claimant an AMTI understatement that costs the government NOTHING on the AMT itself still costs it 26-28 cents on the dollar of the missing add-back. Worked, on the residuals below: a single filer with $200,000 of wages and a $100,000 Schedule C net profit hiding a $20,000 AMT depreciation add-back, holding a $50,000 line 21, is allowed $13,941 of credit on the modeled AMTI and $8,741 on the true one - a $5,200 over-allowance, with the AMT at $0 either way. The Schedule C / royalty / K-1 population below is FREE of this arm unless it also claims the credit, for whom the same understatement has this second, non-zero consequence.
ARM 1 IS THE CLAIM FLAG ANDed WITH THE PRESENCE OF ONE OF FIVE SURFACED-RESIDUAL INTAKES, each an IsComplete-guarded complete-safe gate, with the claim flag as the All's FIRST conjunct so the non-claiming population short-circuits without consulting any of them: - scheduleC:/claimsScheduleCIncome AND scheduleC:/anyScheduleCMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems (residual (b)): line 31 net collapses depreciation, section 179 and vehicle expense into one figure with no method or asset-type distinction; the attestation covers every Form 6251 item that collapse could hide (depreciation, section 179 or amortization, depletion, circulation/research-and-experimental/mining/intangible-drilling costs, section 169 pollution-control amortization, long-term contracts). Complete-safe TRUE: an unanswered attestation, an unanswered /scheduleCs collection, a partially answered return, and a two-business return where only one business attests, all keep the refusal - this conjunct cannot release anyone who has not said so. A return that attests absence while answering Form 8829 line 42 above $0 has contradicted itself and is resolved AGAINST the attestation, in scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems. The attestation is a single whole-business Boolean, not a line-2l-only figure, so residual (b) - the Schedule C depreciation-METHOD detail - stays open for the claimant whose Schedule C carries depreciation: a coarser absence-attestation cannot substitute for method detail. - scheduleE:/claimsRoyaltyIncome AND scheduleE:/royaltyMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems (residual (c), the percentage-depletion half): section 57(a)(1) percentage depletion has its own AMT-item field, /writableRoyaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment, reaching Form 6251 line 2d through /amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment. Complete-safe TRUE on the scheduleE side: an unanswered field or an unanswered royalty section keeps the refusal. - scheduleE:/claimsK1Income AND /anyK1MayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems, and scheduleE:/claimsEstateTrustK1 AND /anyEstateTrustK1MayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems (residual (c), the K-1 half): a per-K-1 coverage instrument - a K-1 whose every answered AMT-items slot is one of the routed codes (A, B or C for a partnership/S-corp K-1; A for an estate/trust K-1) no longer holds its conjunct open, while an unanswered K-1 section, a K-1 recorded for identity boxes only, or a K-1 answering an unrouted code (D, E, F, or a 1041 box-12 code B-F), all keep it open. Each routed code reaches its matching Form 6251 line as a CollectionSum preferred over the filer-typed whole-line attestation, which stays the fallback behind it: box 17/15 code A to line 2l (/amtLine2lDepreciationAfter1986), code B to line 2k (/amtLine2kDispositionOfProperty), code C to line 2d (/amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment), and the 1041 box-12 code A to line 2j (/amtLine2jEstateOrTrustAmtAdjustment). - scheduleE:/claimsFarmRentalIncome AND its own disclosure, /writableAmtLine2lAdjustmentFromFarmRental (a single return-level attestation, since Form 4835 has no per-property collection of its own): Form 4835 enters as an ATTESTED NET, the same collapse as Schedule C.
THREE SCHEDULE E SURFACES ARE DELIBERATELY OUT of this list: a building-only rental is straight-line at either recovery period and carries NO AMT depreciation adjustment (arm 2's own finding); /claimsRemicResidualInterest is MODELED, its section 860E excess inclusion entering AMTI through scheduleE:/scheduleERemicExcessInclusion; and /claimsFarmingFishingIncome is a gross-income attestation for the section 6654 farmer rule that is itself ORed from farm rental, carrying no income intake of its own.
(2) scheduleE:/anyRentalHasAmtDepreciationAdjustment - a rental with a NON-straight-line depreciation intake (a 5-year MACRS personal-property item depreciated 200% DB, incl. its bonus/section 179 sub-elections - Form 6251 line 2l/3 - OR an opaque-method depreciation override) - AND Any(the return is in the AMT-exposed zone (line 6, /amtBaseOverExemption, greater than 0), claims the prior-year minimum tax credit). A building-only rental, a plain Schedule C, an SE / passthrough with only ordinary income, an estate/trust or partnership K-1, and a royalty carry NO modeled AMT-adjustment intake, so they are not refused here - they compute AMT (correctly, usually $0) - UNLESS the return also claims the prior-year minimum tax credit, which is arm 1 above. The exposure conjunct's ordinary-return ground: a 5-year-property rental whose MODELED AMTI is at or below the exemption owes no AMT on that tiny base, so refusing it would be pure over-refusal with no World-#1 benefit (a bonus- or section 179-only property has no AMT depreciation adjustment at all). THAT GROUND FAILS FOR THE PRIOR-YEAR-MTC CLAIMANT, for the reason arm 1 protects: the claimant reads line 9 as Form 8801 line 23, so an understated AMTI buys an overstated credit even where the AMT is zero - which is why the exposure conjunct also opens on the credit claim. The gate is complete-safe (IsComplete guard), so a partial-computation scenario leaves this knockout Complete-false.
A PER-PROPERTY DISCLOSURE NARROWS ARM 2: /anyRentalMayCarryUnmodeledAmtDepreciation and /rentalProperties/*/writableAmtDepreciationAdjustmentFromThisRental - a flagged rental property that has disclosed its own line 2l amount no longer holds arm 2 open. Every disclosure writable in this knockout (the farm-rental and rental Dollars above) is a DISCLOSURE gate, not a magnitude test: stating $0 releases exactly as a nonzero amount does WHEN NOTHING ELSE ON THE RETURN CONTRADICTS IT - what the guard needs is proof the filer was asked and answered, not proof the answer is large. A disclosure must not silently override a different whole-line attestation on the same return: /amtLine2lDepreciationAfter1986 resolves INCOMPLETE rather than silently preferring either side when the attestation and a disclosed source disagree (see that fact's own Description). /formK1s/*/writableK1ReportsNoAmtItems and its Form 1041 twin let a filer attest that a K-1's AMT-items box is genuinely blank instead of typing a code she never saw, releasing ../k1MayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems the same way a routed-slots-only K-1 does.
ARM 2 COUPLES WITH LINE 2g. Specified private activity bond interest (line 2g) is COMPUTED, by /amtLine2gPrivateActivityBondInterest, a summand of /amtiBeforeMfsAddback, rather than knocked out whole upstream: interest:/flowKnockoutHasBonds is a box-8/box-9 consistency gate, so a box 9 covered by its own box 8 reaches this form on a submittable return. Because line 2g raises AMTI, and AMTI raises /amtBaseOverExemption (arm 2's AMT-exposure gate), a box-9 amount can carry a 5-year-property rental filer from at-or-below the exemption to above it and newly refuse a return this knockout would otherwise let through. For that filer the outcome is a refusal either way and only the STATED REASON changes, which is the World-#1-safe direction: the return carries an unmodeled line 2l/3 depreciation adjustment and is refused for exactly that, rather than for holding a bond whose preference this form computes. WHAT STILL REFUSES. The Schedule C conjunct's attestation (scheduleC:/anyScheduleCMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems) is a single whole-business Boolean covering every Form 6251 item the collapsed line-31 total could hide - depreciation, section 179, amortization, depletion, circulation/research-and-experimental/mining/ intangible-drilling costs, section 169 pollution-control amortization, and long-term contracts - not a line-2l-only figure, so a business cannot disclose $0 on depreciation while staying silent on depletion or IDC; residual (b), the Schedule C depreciation-METHOD detail, stays open for the claimant whose Schedule C carries depreciation. A K-1 or estate/trust K-1 answering only an unrouted code, and a claimant who has not opened the K-1/estate-trust-K-1/farm-rental/rental sections at all, still refuse. A royalty working interest's section 57(a)(2) intangible drilling cost preference (Form 6251 line 2t) has no source-side intake - only the filer-typed whole-line attestation /writableAmtLine2tIntangibleDrillingCosts, and a blank attestation is not an attestation of absence, exactly as a blank K-1 box 17 is not - so a royalty depletion answer alone buys a working-interest holder nothing; she is deliberately not even asked (a clean follow-on unit, not foreclosed).
FOUR NAMED LIMITATIONS, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN SILENCED. (1) The K-1 coverage instrument tests ANSWERED slots, not PRINTED items: a partnership K-1 whose paper box 17 carries four AMT-item lines against only three printed slots (i1065sk1 1574-1606) cannot record its fourth item at all, and a filer who enters code A in slot 1 and leaves slots 2-3 blank is released even if the paper also showed D and E; the per-K-1 blank-box attestations answer a DIFFERENT question (nothing is printed) and do not cover it. (2) scheduleE:/writableRoyaltyExpenses collapses Schedule E line 18 ("Depreciation expense OR depletion"), so a royalty carrying post-1986 depreciation in that collapsed figure has a section 56(a)(1) line 2l adjustment with no intake - a scheduleE.xml gap, not a form6251 one. (3) A filer who answers only a new Dollar (farm-rental or rental) and never the whole-line attestation gets the amount inside AMTI and a BLANK printed line 2l (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS6251/en/configuration.yml, f1_16[0]), so printed Part I does not foot; a pdf-binding fix is out of grant. (4) The estate/trust narrowing may release nearly nobody: 1041 box 12 codes B-F are the code-A adjustment's OWN rate-category sub-allocations (f1041sk1 143-164 - qualified dividends, net STCG, net LTCG, unrecaptured section 1250 gain, 28%-rate gain), so a trust K-1 that prints a real AMT adjustment alongside any capital gain normally prints A AND B-F together, which the coverage instrument reads as unrouted and keeps refusing; the safe (over-refusal) direction holds, but the released population is closer to "code-A-only K-1s" than it might appear, unsized.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 6251 Part III lines 13 through 15 must be refigured for the AMT
Fact.Description: Your alternative minimum taxable income is above the exemption (Form 6251 line 6 is more than zero), and your return reports a disposition whose gain or loss is different for the alternative minimum tax (a nonzero Form 6251 line 2k, or a Schedule D line 19 amount refigured for the AMT that differs from the regular tax amount), or a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) with a box 12 amount under code B, C, D, E or F. Form 6251 Part III lines 13, 14 and 15 must then be completed from an AMT Schedule D and AMT capital gain worksheets refigured with your AMT basis. This return cannot prepare those refigured worksheets, so it cannot be filed here. A return whose line 6 is zero does not reach Part III and is not affected.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 11 - Alternative Minimum Tax (Schedule 2 line 2)
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 11 = line 9 minus the regular tax for the AMT (line 10), floored at 0 — read straight off the printed line, "AMT. Subtract line 10 from line 9". Line 9 is its own fact, /amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftc, which 2025 Form 8801 line 23 also reads. Line 9 carries no Round, so no intermediate rounding is introduced between the two subtractions and (l7 - l8) - l10 is exactly l7 - (l8 + l10). Line 9 = line 7 - line 8 = tentative minimum tax - /amtForeignTaxCredit, so this chain removes BOTH /amtForeignTaxCredit (line 8) and /amtRegularTaxForComparison (line 10) from /tentativeMinimumTax (line 7). Because line 8 and line 10 both subtract the SAME Schedule 3 line 1 foreign tax credit, the credit CANCELS (line 11 = TMT - regular): if line 8 were forced to 0 instead, the uncancelled line-10 FTC subtraction would overstate the AMT by exactly the foreign tax credit, overcharging a 904(j) FTC-electing filer who owes AMT up to $600/$300. Flows to Schedule 2 (Form 1040) line 2. Zero whenever the tentative minimum tax does not exceed the regular tax - the common case. A return knocked out by /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference or /knockoutAmtPart3RefigureUnbuilt contributes 0 here: it cannot be filed, and the 0 keeps every existing Schedule C / Schedule E golden additive-clean while the knockout is what actually refuses the return. COMPLETE-SAFE (the form8960 pattern): resolves Complete-0 on any partial-computation scenario where the AMTI or the regular-tax-for-comparison input is Incomplete (e.g. an eligibility golden whose /taxableIncome or regular tax never resolves), so this fact — and Schedule 2 line 3 (/totalAdditionalTaxesOwed) built on it — never drops from its prior completeness.

Fact.Name: A Form 1116 credit on a return where the AMT foreign tax credit reaches a dollar
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when the return takes its foreign tax credit from Form 1116 and the AMT foreign tax credit can change a dollar on the return. Form 6251 line 8 must be the AMT foreign tax credit, figured on a separate AMT Form 1116 for each category of income. This dictionary builds no AMT Form 1116, so on a Form 1116 return line 8 carries the regular Form 1116 credit (Schedule 3 line 1), and line 9 and everything that reads it can be wrong in either direction, with no dollar cap.
FIRES WHEN all three hold: (1) Schedule 3 line 1 is the Form 1116 credit: the no-Form-1116 exception does not apply and the filer opened Form 1116 (foreignTaxCredit /qualifiesForNoForm1116Exception Complete false, form1116 /form1116Answered true). This is schedule3 /sched3Line1's own Form 1116 selector. (2) Form 6251 line 7 is above zero. At zero, line 9 floored at zero is zero whatever line 8 is, and line 11 is zero, so no AMT foreign tax credit can move a dollar. (3) /requiresForm6251 is true. Its statement 1 (line 7 above line 10) is where the AMT itself depends on line 8; its statements 2 and 3 (a Form 3800 general business credit, the Form 8801 credit, the Form 8834 credit or the personal part of the Form 8911 credit) are the credit limits that read /amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftcFloored. With none of them true, line 8 reaches no dollar: line 11 is zero because line 9 is at most line 7, which is at most line 10. One print-only gap: Form 3800 line 14 is filled on any general business credit return, but statement 2 fires only when Form 3800 line 6 is above zero; with line 6 at zero the printed line 14 may rest on the regular credit, and no dollar moves (line 17 is the smaller of line 6 and line 16). The no-Form-1116 election is not refused: there the AMT foreign tax credit is the Schedule 3 line 1 credit by the instructions' own rule.
IsComplete first on every leg: a return with no foreign tax, or one that never opened Form 1116, resolves Complete false.
SCREEN: "Your return takes its foreign tax credit from Form 1116, and your return also needs the alternative minimum tax figures (Form 6251). The AMT foreign tax credit must be figured on a separate AMT Form 1116, which this return cannot prepare yet. You can't file this return here."

Fact.Name: Form 6251 lines 2c through 3, combined
Fact.Description: The total of Form 6251 lines 2c through 3, signed as printed: line 4 before the married-filing-separately addition, less line 1b, less line 2a, plus the line 2b amount (which line 4 subtracts). Negative when the negative adjustments among lines 2c through 3 outweigh the positive ones.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 4 figured without lines 2c through 3 (Who Must File statement 4)
Fact.Description: Line 4 as it would be if lines 2c through 3 were not taken into account: line 1b plus line 2a less the line 2b amount, plus the married-filing-separately addition figured on that amount the way line 4's instruction figures it (25 percent of the excess over $900,350, at most $68,500).

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 6 figured without lines 2c through 3 (Who Must File statement 4)
Fact.Description: Line 6 on /amtStatement4Line4WithoutLines2cThrough3: that amount less the line 5 exemption figured on it (the same exemption amount and phase-out threshold, reduced by 25 percent of the excess over the threshold), never below zero.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 7 at the 26 and 28 percent rates, figured without lines 2c through 3 (Who Must File statement 4)
Fact.Description: The 26 percent and 28 percent tax on /amtStatement4Line6WithoutLines2cThrough3, with the same breakpoint and adjustment line 7 uses. Line 7 is never more than this amount (Part III, when it applies, takes the smaller figure), so this is an upper bound on line 7 without lines 2c through 3 and equals it on a return that does not complete Part III.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 Who Must File statement 4 applies (read with the 26 and 28 percent bound)
Fact.Description: True when the total of lines 2c through 3 is negative and line 7 figured without them, at the 26 and 28 percent rates, is greater than line 10. On a return that does not complete Part III that is exactly statement 4. On a return that does, line 7 without lines 2c through 3 could be smaller than the flat-rate figure, so this can also be true where statement 4 is not: Form 6251 is then attached though the instructions do not require it, which changes no amount. False whenever the lines 2c through 3 total, the flat-rate figure or line 10 does not resolve.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 filing requirement (Who Must File)
Fact.Description:
Whether Form 6251 must be completed and attached to the return, per the 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 "Who Must File" (attach Form 6251 if any of four statements is true). INFORMATIONAL / completeness only - it is NOT a submission gate and knocks nothing out. All four statements are disjuncts here: (1) line 7 (tentative minimum tax) is greater than line 10 (regular tax for the AMT). Modeled directly as the line 7/line 10 comparison (/tentativeMinimumTax greater than /amtRegularTaxForComparison) to stay faithful to the worksheet text and to remain true even for a return whose /alternativeMinimumTax is force-zeroed by a scope-out knockout. NOTE: because line 8 (AMTFTC = Schedule 3 line 1, /amtForeignTaxCredit) can be nonzero, statement 1 is deliberately BROADER than "owes AMT" (line 11 > 0): the AMT is line 9 - line 10 = (line 7 - line 8) - line 10, so a filer with line 10 < line 7 <= line 10 + line 8 must file Form 6251 (statement 1 true) yet owes no AMT. That is the form's own text - statement 1 compares line 7 to line 10 directly, never line 9 - so it is left unchanged. (2) the return claims a general business credit and Form 3800 Part I line 6 or line 25 is more than zero. Read as form3800 /form3800Line6 more than $0, IsComplete-first, so a line 6 that is Incomplete (a transferred-in credit awaiting Form 8582-CR) leaves this disjunct false rather than blanking the fact. A positive line 6 is itself a general business credit on Part I, so it carries the first half of the statement. Line 25 (Section B, lines 22 plus 24) is $0 on every return this dictionary represents: Section B is completed only for an empowerment zone or renewal community employment credit on Part III line 3, and no Part III line 3 fact exists (form3800 /form3800Line28 states the same boundary), so line 6 is the whole of statement 2 here. (3) the return claims the credit for prior year minimum tax (Form 8801, /claimsPriorYearMinimumTaxCredit), the qualified electric vehicle credit (form8834 /form8834Applies) or the personal-use part of the alternative fuel vehicle refueling property credit (form8911 /form8911PersonalPartApplies). (4) the total of lines 2c through 3 is negative and line 7 would exceed line 10 without them: /amtWhoMustFileStatement4, which figures lines 4 through 6 again without lines 2c through 3 and line 7 at the 26 and 28 percent rates. That flat-rate line 7 is an upper bound (Part III only lowers line 7), so on a return that completes Part III the disjunct can be true where the statement is not and Form 6251 is then attached though not required; it is never false where the statement is true. A return that owes no AMT but claims the prior-year MTC still "requires" Form 6251 to substantiate that credit, which is why this is informational and independent of /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference (that knockout separately refuses the prior-year-MTC return from being filed at all). COMPLETE-SAFE: resolves on every return via the IsComplete guards on the line 7/line 10 comparison, the same pattern /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference uses; /claimsPriorYearMinimumTaxCredit is itself complete-safe.
DISPOSITION: EXPORTED as a CULMINATING fact. Re-measured on this trunk: no fact's depends_on in dictionary/manifest/facts-manifest.json names this path, no syndoc workbook lists it in a required VALUE_FACTS tuple, and no flow gate reads it — which is the fact's own "INFORMATIONAL / completeness only, NOT a submission gate" self-description restated as a measurement. That is precisely a CULMINATING fact: it terminates the computation and its answer is wanted outside the graph, which is what downstreamFacts asserts (js/src/TaxLogicTestCoverageReporter.ts reads that flag as `culminating`). The claim is TRUE rather than circular because the value is a REAL OUTPUT: the printed 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 pose "Who Must File" as a question to the filer, and this fact is the answer — whether Form 6251 must be completed and ATTACHED to the return. Before this Export the attachment requirement could not leave the dictionary at all.
THIS IS downstreamFacts, NOT mef="true". /requiresSchedule1 and /requiresSchedule2 carry Export mef="true" as part of their verbatim L0 vendoring copy, so their mef is UPSTREAM's claim about the MeF binding layer, not a claim this repo derived; mef also asserts the IRS RECEIVES this element, an e-file/MeF schema question project invariant #7 excludes from this repo and invariant #3 leaves unsettleable from anything in sources/. downstreamFacts claims only what is measurable from the graph plus the printed instruction, so that is what is claimed here.
The Export changes no resolved value: it is metadata on the Fact element, absent from the manifest schema (completeness/depends_on/module/rounding/type/writable) and from the baseline row shape (path/completeness/type/value). NO NODE TEST PINS THIS PATH — that gap is real and is NOT closed by this disposition; the Export makes it VISIBLE instead, because a culminating fact with no test now appears in the coverage reporter's untested-culminating column rather than being invisible to it. scripts/test_lint_wiring.py pins the Export itself, since a fact that loses its Export with no skip row left behind falls straight back to UNWIRED with nothing to catch it.

Fact.Name: 2024 Form 6251 line 11, the prior-year AMT (carry-IN attestation)
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 16: "Enter the amount from your 2024 Form 6251, line 11, or 2024 Schedule I (Form 1041), line 54". A PRIOR-YEAR figure this single-year graph cannot compute (the engine holds no cross-year state), so it is ATTESTED by the filer, the same carry-IN posture as /writableNonrecapturedSection1231Loss and /writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear. NON-NEGATIVE by the printed fence on the source line itself: 2024 Form 6251 line 11 is "AMT. Subtract line 10 from line 9. If zero or less, enter -0-", so the figure it carries can never be negative. OPTIONAL: unanswered means no prior-year AMT, which the complete-safe wrapper below renders as 0.
NAMING (the intake side). Its emit-side twin is a TY2024 dictionary's own /alternativeMinimumTax, the same Form 6251 line 11 this repo already computes for TY2025; an ordinary pairing the lint will find once two year dictionaries coexist.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 16 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /writableAlternativeMinimumTaxFromPriorTaxYear when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means the filer paid no AMT in 2024, so there is no minimum tax credit to carry in. ALWAYS COMPLETE, which is load-bearing rather than tidy: this fact feeds line 18, line 21 and ultimately Schedule 3 line 7, and an Incomplete here would take /totalOtherNonrefundableCredits Incomplete with it and REMOVE a committed row on every return.

Fact.Name: 2024 net minimum tax on exclusion items, Form 8801 Part I line 15 (carry-IN attestation)
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 lines 15 and 17. Line 15 is Part I's output, "Net minimum tax on exclusion items. Subtract line 14 from line 13. If zero or less, enter -0-"; line 17 is "Enter the amount from line 15". ONE fact serves both printed lines because the form itself makes line 17 a copy of line 15.
WHY IT IS ATTESTED RATHER THAN COMPUTED, and this is the structural decision of the whole unit, not a convenience. Part I recomputes the PRIOR year's tentative minimum tax on EXCLUSION ITEMS ONLY - a second, differently-parameterised AMT run over a year this dictionary does not hold. Attesting its output means Part I is not built, and because Form 8801 Part III is entered only through Part I line 11, Part III is not reached either. NON-NEGATIVE by line 15's own printed "If zero or less, enter -0-". OPTIONAL: unanswered means 0.
NAMING: this intake has NO emit-side twin and cannot have one. A TY2024 dictionary computes TY2024's ORDINARY AMT, never TY2024's exclusion-items-only AMT, so the pairing lint armed at TY2026's arrival must treat this path as a PERMANENT exception rather than a missing twin.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 14 (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableForm8801Line14PriorYearRegularTaxForTheAmtComparison when the filer entered it, else $0: the 2024 Form 6251 line 10 regular tax that line 15 subtracts from line 13. The complete safe wrapper line 15 needs, so that a filer who worked Part I but left this optional box blank still gets a line 15 rather than an Incomplete one. Unanswered means no 2024 regular tax to measure the exclusion items tentative tax against, which makes line 15 the whole of line 13, the conservative direction for the credit (a LARGER line 17 is subtracted at line 18, so the credit is smaller). NO PRINTED BOX MAPS THIS FACT; the writable maps line 14.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 15 before its zero fence
Fact.Description: Line 13 minus line 14, before the printed "If zero or less, enter -0-" is applied. NO PRINTED BOX MAPS IT; the floored sibling maps line 15.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 15, the computed net minimum tax on exclusion items
Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 15 = line 13 minus line 14, floored at zero by the printed "If zero or less, enter -0-". This is the OUTPUT OF PART I and, through line 17, the subtrahend of line 18, so it is the figure the whole minimum tax credit chain is measured against. NO PRINTED BOX MAPS THIS FACT directly; the register maps line 15 through /netMinimumTaxOnExclusionItemsFromPriorTaxYear, which selects between this fact and the attestation /writableNetMinimumTaxOnExclusionItemsFromPriorTaxYear.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 lines 15 and 17, computed from Part I when Part I was worked
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 15, repeated at line 17 and subtracted at line 18. COMPUTED FROM PART I, with the attestation kept behind it.
FIRST ARM. When /form8801Line13TentativeMinimumTaxOnExclusionItems is Complete, this fact is the computed /form8801Line15NetMinimumTaxOnExclusionItems. IsComplete on line 13 is a REAL "was Part I worked" predicate and not a formality: line 13 is line 11 less line 12, and line 11 is Incomplete unless the filer either worked Part III or answered enough of lines 1 through 6 for line 10 to resolve, so on a return that never opened Form 8801 Part I this arm cannot fire.
SECOND ARM. Otherwise /writableNetMinimumTaxOnExclusionItemsFromPriorTaxYear when answered: the filer's transcription of their own 2024 Form 8801 line 15.
THIRD ARM. Otherwise $0. Unanswered means no prior year minimum tax on exclusion items, so the whole of line 16 is creditable at line 18. ALWAYS COMPLETE, for the same reason its line 16 sibling is.
WHAT THIS REACHES. Lines 1 through 15 of Part I, and every one of the twenty-odd Part III lines behind line 11, reach /form8801Line18PriorYearAmtOverExclusionItems, /form8801Line21MinimumTaxCreditAvailable, /form8801MinimumTaxCreditAllowed and Schedule 3 line 6b.

Fact.Name: 2024 Form 8801 line 26 credit carryforward (carry-IN attestation)
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 19: "2024 credit carryforward. Enter the amount from your 2024 Form 8801, line 26". The unused remainder of every earlier year's minimum tax credit. NON-NEGATIVE by the printed construction of its source line: 2024 line 26 is line 21 minus line 25, and line 25 is the smaller of line 21 or line 24 with line 24 floored at zero, so line 26 can never be negative. OPTIONAL: unanswered means 0.
NAMING, AND ITS TWIN IS IN THIS SAME FILE. The emit-side twin is /minimumTaxCreditCarryforwardToNextYear below - this form's own line 26, and why the emit side is authored in the SAME unit as this intake.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 19 (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /writableMinimumTaxCreditCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means no unused credit was carried into 2025. ALWAYS COMPLETE, for the same reason its two siblings are.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 18 - prior-year AMT in excess of the exclusion-items minimum tax
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 18 = line 16 minus line 17: "Subtract line 17 from line 16. If less than zero, enter as a negative amount".
DELIBERATELY NOT FLOORED, and the printed instruction is unusually explicit about it. Every neighbouring line on this form carries a zero fence; this one carries the opposite instruction. A floor here would raise line 21 for a filer whose prior-year AMT was driven entirely by exclusion items, granting a credit the statute does not allow - taxpayer- favourable in the wrong direction and contrary to the printed form. The floor that does exist is line 21's stop rule, one line later.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 21 - the minimum tax credit available before this year's tax limit
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 21 = "Combine lines 18 through 20". Line 20 (the 2024 unallowed qualified electric vehicle credit) is a DOCUMENTED ZERO with no writable and no intake - a pre-2009 provision, see the section header - so the combine is line 18 plus line 19.
THE CLAIM GATE RIDES HERE, and this is the one place in the chain where a gate is placed rather than inherited. A filer who does not claim the prior-year minimum tax credit does not complete Form 8801 at all, so zero is this line's FAITHFUL value for them, not a conservative stand-in. Placing the gate at line 21 rather than at lines 25 and 26 separately is what the form's own stop rule already does: "If line 21 is zero or less, you don't have a minimum tax credit or a credit carryforward", which couples both outputs to this single line. ITS SECOND JOB HAS ENDED. While the blanket /claimsPriorYearMinimumTaxCredit arm of /knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference stood, this gate was what made "a non-zero credit implies a refused return" true by construction; the arm is now narrowed and that implication is deliberately false - a claimant with no unmodeled-adjustment intake gets the credit on a filable return. What the gate still does is its FIRST job, unchanged and unconditional. NOT FLOORED: line 21 is legitimately negative when the prior-year AMT was smaller than its exclusion-items component, and the smaller-of at line 25 needs to see that (the floor is applied there, once).

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 22 - 2025 regular income tax liability minus allowable credits
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 22 = (Form 1040 line 16 + Schedule 2 line 1z) minus (Form 1040 line 19 + Schedule 3 lines 1 through 6z, EXCLUDING the line 6b prior-year minimum tax credit). That is the instruction read literally: "Add the amounts from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16 and Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 1z. Subtract from the result the total of any credits from Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 19 and Schedule 3 (Form 1040), lines 1 through 6z (not including any credit for prior year minimum tax on line 6b or any credit claimed on Form 8912, Credit to Holders of Tax Credit Bonds, on line 6k). Enter the result. If the result is zero or less, enter -0-".
THAT INSTRUCTION IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO PLACES IN THE VENDORED EXTRACTION, and reading only the first half gets the line wrong. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8801.pdf, page 4 carry the sentence up to "or any credit claimed on Form 8912," and stop at the bottom of a printed column; the tail, "Credit to Holders of Tax Credit Bonds, on line 6k). Enter the result. If the result is zero or less, enter -0-.", is at lines 221-222, where the two-column pdftotext pass deposited it seventy lines EARLIER. Both halves are cited below. This is recorded because the missing tail carried the zero floor, and a build that read only lines 283-291 would have built an unfloored line 22.
THE 6b EXCLUSION IS WHAT KEEPS THE GRAPH ACYCLIC, not a rounding detail. This credit lands on Schedule 3 line 6b, which flows into line 7 and then line 8; if this line subtracted /line8OfSchedule3 the graph would close the loop 6b to line 7 to line 8 to line 22 to line 24 to line 25 to 6b. Subtracting line 8 and adding 6b back does NOT help - the values cancel but the dependency EDGE remains, and the Fact Graph resolves on edges, not on algebra. So it reads schedule3:/sched3CreditsThrough6zExcluding6b, a named 6b-free subtotal built for this purpose in the same commit.
THE FORM 1040 LINE-19 TERM IS ctcOdc:/totalCtcAndOdc, which already ships exported and needed no edit - the handoff design that named ctcOdc.xml as a second blocked file was re-derived on this tree and is false. It carries no 6b dependency either: Credit Limit Worksheet A line 2 sums Schedule 3 lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5b, 6d, 6f, 6l and 6m, and Worksheet B line 15 sums lines 5a, 6c, 6g and 6h. Line 6b appears in NEITHER, checked on disk against https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, pages 4, 6, so the CTC/ODC cannot close a loop through this line.
FLOORED AT ZERO, AND THE F81 CONTRACT SAID OTHERWISE. Its prerequisite (2b) gave two independent reasons why /amtRegularTaxForComparison could not serve as this line's base: the double-subtraction of the foreign tax credit, and "THE FLOOR ... 8801 line 22 prints NO floor; the floor on that side of the form is at line 24". THE SECOND REASON IS FALSE, and it is false for exactly the reason recorded above: the line-22 instruction's own "If the result is zero or less, enter -0-" sits at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8801.pdf, page 4, seventy lines away from the rest of its sentence, and reading only the contiguous span misses it. This fact therefore floors, as the instruction says.
THE FIRST REASON STILL STANDS ALONE AND IS WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FACT. Form 6251 line 10 subtracts Schedule 3 line 1 and NOTHING ELSE; line 22 subtracts Form 1040 line 19 and the whole of Schedule 3 lines 1 through 6z. Line 1 is inside that span, so using line 10 as this line's base and then subtracting the 6b-free subtotal would remove the foreign tax credit TWICE - understating line 22, understating line 24, and cutting the credit.
DIRECTION OF THE FLOOR, since it is a correction rather than an original reading: without it, a negative line 22 propagates into line 24 as line 22 minus line 23, which is strictly LESS than the floored form's zero minus line 23. So the unfloored version could only ever UNDER-allow the credit. Taxpayer-adverse.
IS THE FLOOR REACHABLE? STATED WITH ITS ROUTES AND ITS REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, the form8863 line-6 pattern, because "no captured row reaches it" asserts much less than it looks like it does. IT HAS NO WITNESS TODAY: zero of the 942 captured rows and none of this change's five node tests reach it, so deleting the GreaterOf leaves the whole suite green. That is stated first because it is the honest status of the arm.
THE STRUCTURAL ROUTE THAT LOOKS OPEN, AND WHY IT IS CLOSED IN WHOLE DOLLARS. Credit Limit Worksheet A line 2 sums Schedule 3 lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5b, 6d, 6f, 6l and 6m - it OMITS 5a, 6c and 6g - while this line's subtrahend includes them. So ctcOdc:/totalCtcAndOdc can consume a tax capacity computed without those three, and this line then subtracts them ON TOP. The gap is not closed by Credit Limit Worksheet B either, whose trigger needs Schedule 8812 line 4 greater than zero, i.e. a qualifying child under 17: an OTHER-DEPENDENTS-ONLY filer with a nonzero 6c or 6g is not a Worksheet B filer at all. What closes it is that each of those three credits carries its OWN limit worksheet, and each of those subtracts Form 1040 line 19 - the CTC/ODC - from its capacity. So on the non-Worksheet-B arm 5a, 6c and 6g are already capped at the capacity remaining AFTER the ODC, and in whole-dollar arithmetic line 19 plus the Schedule 3 subtotal cannot exceed 1040 line 16 plus Schedule 2 line 1z. This is exactly the argument form8863's line-6 comment records for its own floor, and it fails in the same two places.
WHAT SURVIVES, both of them narrow. (a) THE HALF_UP OVERSHOOT: ctcOdc:/totalCtcAndOdc is Round()ed while the capacity it is capped by is not, so a limit binding at a cents value rounds UP to as much as $0.50 above the capacity actually remaining, and every bridge credit then sizes itself against that inflated line 19. Sub-dollar, needs a cents-bearing input, and it is the same permanent consequence of the round-at-the-printed-line convention that form8863's route (a) records. (b) SCHEDULE 3 LINE 6h (Form 8859), which has no module and no intake: it is absent from this line's subtrahend AND from Worksheet A line 2, so it cannot open the route by itself - but it is also absent from Worksheet B line 15, which is the disclosed residue ctcOdc:/sched8812CreditLimit already carries, and through that path a short line 15 raises the CTC/ODC and lowers this line.
SO THE FLOOR IS DEFENCE IN DEPTH PLUS A LIVE SUB-DOLLAR CORRECTION, and it is the PRINTED instruction either way, which is the whole of its justification. The REJECTED ALTERNATIVE is the one the previous commit shipped: leave the line unfloored on the strength of the F81 contract's "8801 line 22 prints NO floor". That reading rested on a truncated cite span, and an unfloored line can only cut the credit.
LINE 6k IS EXCLUDED TOO, and by absence rather than by construction: the parenthesis also excludes "any credit claimed on Form 8912, Credit to Holders of Tax Credit Bonds, on line 6k", and this dictionary models no Form 8912 and declares no /sched3Line6k, so the subtotal this line subtracts carries no 6k term to remove. A documented zero of the same class as line 20.
NOT ROUNDED: the rounding for this chain happens once, at line 25.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 24 - this year's regular tax capacity for the minimum tax credit
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 24 = "Subtract line 23 from line 22. If zero or less, enter -0-". Line 23 is "the amount from your 2025 Form 6251, line 9", which ships as /amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftcFloored - line 7 minus the line-8 AMTFTC, floored at zero, NOT line 7 and NOT the floored line 11. Reading line 7 here would overstate line 23 by exactly the foreign tax credit and cut the credit. The zero floor keeps a negative line 9 from lifting this line above line 22 (see /amtLine9TentativeMinimumTaxAfterAmtftcFloored).
THIS IS THE ECONOMIC CONTENT OF THE WHOLE FORM: a filer may use the prior-year minimum tax credit only to the extent this year's regular tax exceeds this year's tentative minimum tax. A filer who owes AMT again this year has line 22 at or below line 23 and this line floors to zero, so no credit is allowed - correctly.
THE FLOOR IS THE PRINTED ONE and it is the only floor between line 22 and line 25.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 25 - the credit for prior year minimum tax (Schedule 3 line 6b)
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 25 = "Minimum tax credit. Enter the smaller of line 21 or line 24. Also enter this amount on your 2025 Schedule 3 (Form 1040), line 6b". Wired to schedule3:/sched3Line6b in the same commit, so the credit reaches the return rather than being computed and dropped.
NON-NEGATIVE, and the zero floor is the stop rule rather than an invention. Line 24 is already floored at zero, so the smaller-of can only go negative when line 21 does - and the printed instruction for that case is "If line 21 is zero or less, you don't have a minimum tax credit or a credit carryforward", i.e. exactly zero. The GreaterOf below IS that sentence. ROUNDED HERE, ONCE. Lines 18 through 24 are left unrounded so that no intermediate rounding is introduced into a chain whose terms already carry cents (line 22's minuend is the unrounded 1040 line 16 plus Schedule 2 line 1z, and line 23 is deliberately unrounded). Round is HALF_UP to whole dollars, the module convention.
COMPLETE-SAFE, AND THIS IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN DEFENSIVE. Line 24's chain reaches the regular tax and the tentative minimum tax, either of which can be Incomplete on a partial-computation scenario. An Incomplete here would propagate into schedule3:/totalOtherNonrefundableCredits and REMOVE that fact's committed Complete row on every affected case, which is a changed committed row produced by a fact whose VALUE never moved (the rounding-row landmine). The IsComplete guard makes the credit resolve Complete zero instead - the World-#1 direction as well, since a credit that cannot be substantiated is not granted.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 26 - the credit carryforward to 2026
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 26 = "Credit carryforward to 2026. Subtract line 25 from line 21. Keep a record of this amount because you may use it in future years". The unused remainder of the available credit: whatever line 21 offered that this year's tax capacity could not absorb.
THIS IS AN EMIT-SIDE FACT, which is why it is EXPORTED with no in-graph consumer. Item 1 names "the Form 8801 chain's unused-credit remainder" among the figures a year hands forward, and its intake-side twin is /writableMinimumTaxCreditCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear above - the same quantity, one year later. The printed form already says as much ("keep a record ... you may use it in future years"). Authored in the same unit as its intake twin, as item 1 requires.
FLOORED AT ZERO, which is the stop rule again: a non-positive line 21 means "you don't have a minimum tax credit OR a credit carryforward", so a negative line 21 emits 0 rather than a negative carryforward. When line 21 is positive the floor is a no-op, because line 25 is the smaller of line 21 and a non-negative line 24 and therefore never exceeds line 21.
ALWAYS COMPLETE: line 21 and line 25 are both complete-safe, so nothing here can go Incomplete. WHEN LINE 24 IS INCOMPLETE the credit resolves 0 and this fact emits the WHOLE of line 21 - which is the correct answer, not a fallback: nothing was used, so everything carries forward.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2b, the tax refund not included in AMTI
Fact.Description: Form 6251 line 2b = Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 1, the taxable refund of state and local income taxes (income:/taxableStateAndLocalIncomeTaxRefunds). The printed box is parenthesized: because the tax that produced the refund was never deductible for the AMT, IRC 56(b)(1)(C) keeps the recovery out of alternative minimum taxable income, so the amount is answered POSITIVE here and SUBTRACTED by whatever total consumes it, exactly as line 2f is. The line 8z leg of the printed alternative is /amtLine2bScheduleOneLine8zTaxRefunds, the refunds the filer states were included in Schedule 1 line 8z and are attributable to state or local personal property or general sales taxes, foreign income taxes, or state, local or foreign real property taxes; it is $0 on every return that states none. Print only until /amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold subtracts it, and the gap is not academic: this fact is nonzero on any return with a taxable state refund, and line 2a has already added the whole SALT or standard deduction back.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2b, the tax refunds included in Schedule 1 line 8z
Fact.Description: The part of the Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 8z write-in entries that is a refund received in 2025 of state or local personal property taxes or general sales taxes, foreign income taxes, or state, local or foreign real property taxes. Form 6251 line 2b takes these together with the Schedule 1 line 1 refund, because the tax refunded was never deductible for the alternative minimum tax. Answered as a POSITIVE amount; the printed parentheses are applied by the total that subtracts line 2b. The instructions also ask for a description and the amount next to the line 2b entry space whenever a line 8z amount is included. Unanswered means no such refund was reported on line 8z.

Fact.Name: Form 6251 line 2b, the Schedule 1 line 8z leg (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableAmtLine2bScheduleOneLine8zTaxRefunds floored at $0 and capped at income:/schedule1Line8zEntriesTotal, the total of the Schedule 1 line 8z write-in entries, because line 2b can only take back a refund that line 8z actually included in income; $0 when unanswered. Fact.Description: Line 27's Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet arm: preferentialRateTax:/qdcgLine5 when the Schedule D Tax Worksheet entry test is NOT met, otherwise $0. Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 12 (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableForm8801Line12ForeignTaxCreditOnExclusionItems when answered, else 0. Unanswered means no foreign tax credit was allowed against the 2024 exclusion items minimum tax. ALWAYS COMPLETE. NO PRINTED BOX MAPS THIS FACT; the writable maps line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 13, the prior year tentative minimum tax on exclusion items
Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 13 = line 11 minus line 12: "Tentative minimum tax on exclusion items." No zero fence is printed on this line; the fence is on line 15, one line later. THE CREDIT CHAIN CONSUMES IT: /form8801Line15NetMinimumTaxOnExclusionItems is this fact less /form8801Line14PriorYearRegularTaxForTheAmtComparisonOrZero, floored at zero, and /netMinimumTaxOnExclusionItemsFromPriorTaxYear selects it whenever THIS fact is Complete, which is the "was Part I worked" predicate. Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 11: 26 percent of the exclusion items base
Fact.Description: The 26 percent arm of Form 8801 line 11, Round(26/100 times /form8801Line10ExclusionItemsBaseOverTheExemption). Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 11: the 28 percent arm after the 2024 bracket adjustment
Fact.Description: The 28 percent arm of Form 8801 line 11: Round(28/100 times line 10) less $4,652, the printed "Otherwise, multiply line 10 by 28% (0.28) and subtract $4,652 ($2,326 if married filing separately for 2024) from the result". This arm is the non married filing separately figure. The $2,326 variant is figured by /form8801Line11TaxByPriorYearStatus when the 2024 status is stated, and /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase reaches this arm only when no 2024 status is stated and no line 11 was typed. NO PRINTED BOX MAPS THIS FACT.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 11, the prior year tentative tax on the exclusion items base, computed
Fact.Description:
Form 8801 line 11, COMPUTED rather than attested. AHEAD OF THE PART III ARM: when /writableForm8801PriorYearFiledForm2555 is true the filer's own line 11 is taken, because the printed line sends a 2024 Form 2555 filer to a worksheet this dictionary does not hold, and line 55 itself says a 2024 Form 2555 filer does not enter it on line 11. RIGHT AFTER THE PART III ARM and before the two described below: when the 2024 filing status is stated (/form8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately), /form8801Line11TaxByPriorYearStatus computes the All others branch with that status's breakpoint and subtraction, which settles the married filing separately band between $116,300 and $232,600 that the second arm below would otherwise take at 26 percent. With neither question answered the arms below apply. THIS IS THE HINGE OF PART I AND PART III: the form reaches Part III only through line 11, so the twenty-odd lines Part III computes and the line 10 base Part I computes both reach line 13. The Switch follows the printed three way branch in the order that keeps every answered return safe.
FIRST ARM, PART III. When /form8801Line55TaxOnExclusionItemsFromPartThree is Complete, line 11 is that figure, which is literally what the printed line 55 says ("Enter the smaller of line 53 or line 54 here and on line 11"). IsComplete on line 55 is a REAL "was Part III worked" predicate, not a formality: line 55 is the lesser of line 53 and the attested line 54, and line 53 sums the attested lines 33 and 46 with the guarded lines 49 and 52, so it is Incomplete on every return that did not work Part III.
SECOND ARM, THE 26 PERCENT BAND WITH NO 2024 STATUS STATED. When line 10 is Complete and at or below $232,600, line 11 is 26 percent of line 10. Below $116,300 both 2024 statuses take 26 percent, so the arm is exact there. Between $116,300 and $232,600 a 2024 married filing separately filer belongs in the 28 percent band less $2,326, and with the status unanswered this arm gives that filer 26 percent, ahead of any typed line 11: the band is settled by /form8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately (the Form 8801 answer, or else the refund worksheet's 2024 filing status) through the status arm above. Direction for that filer while the status is unanswered: line 11 is under-stated, so line 13 and line 15 are under-stated and the credit can be over-stated.
THIRD ARM, THE FILER'S OWN ENTRY. With no 2024 status stated and line 10 above $232,600 or Incomplete, an answered /writableForm8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase above $0 wins. Above $232,600 the two 2024 statuses differ only in the subtraction ($2,326 against $4,652), and the filer's transcription carries the right one. A typed $0 does not win: no rate the form prints gives a $0 tax on a base above $232,600, so it falls to the computed arm below (with line 10 Incomplete it leaves line 11 Incomplete).
FOURTH ARM, THE 28 PERCENT BAND WITH NOTHING TYPED. Only when line 10 is above $232,600, no 2024 status is stated and no line 11 was typed does this fact compute 28 percent of line 10 less $4,652, the non married filing separately figure.
COMPLETENESS. When line 10 is Incomplete and line 11 was answered, the third arm hands back the attestation. When neither is answerable this fact is Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Form 8801, was your 2024 filing status married filing separately
Fact.Description: Whether the filer's 2024 filing status was married filing separately. Form 8801 refigures the 2024 minimum tax, and its lines 11, 33 and 54 choose both the 26 percent breakpoint ($116,300 instead of $232,600) and the 28 percent subtraction ($2,326 instead of $4,652) by the 2024 status, which the current year's filing status does not tell. Answered, it decides /form8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately, which lets /form8801PriorYearAmtRateBreakpoint and /form8801PriorYearAmtRateSubtraction resolve and those three lines be computed for either status; it wins over the refund worksheet's 2024 status (income:/writablePriorYearFilingStatus) when the two disagree. Unanswered, that 2024 status decides when it is answered; with neither answered, the lines resolve by their status free arms: line 11 by its old arms, and lines 33 and 54 computed only where the two statuses agree, otherwise from the filer's own entry, otherwise at the non married filing separately figures.

Fact.Name: Form 8801, did you file Form 2555 for 2024
Fact.Description: Whether the filer filed Form 2555 for 2024. Form 8801 line 11 sends that filer to the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet in the instructions instead of the rate arithmetic, and this dictionary holds no such worksheet, so when this is answered true /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase takes the filer's own /writableForm8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase rather than any computed figure. Unanswered or false leaves line 11 to its other arms.

Fact.Name: Form 8801, the 2024 filing status was married filing separately (the answer the lines use)
Fact.Description: Whether the filer's 2024 filing status was married filing separately, as Form 8801 lines 11, 33 and 54 use it. The Form 8801 question (/writableForm8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately) decides when it is answered. When it is not, the 2024 filing status the filer gave for the state and local refund worksheet (income:/writablePriorYearFilingStatus) decides: married filing separately is true, any other status false. Both questions ask for the same 2024 fact; when both are answered and disagree, the Form 8801 answer wins, because it is the one asked for this computation (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS CR-13). Incomplete when neither is answered, so the lines that read it fall back to their status free arms.

Fact.Name: Form 8801, the 26 percent breakpoint for the 2024 filing status
Fact.Description: The top of the 26 percent band that Form 8801 lines 11, 33 and 54 apply: $116,300 when /form8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately is true, $232,600 when it is false. Incomplete when the 2024 status is unanswered, so the facts that read it fall back to their status free arms.

Fact.Name: Form 8801, the 28 percent band subtraction for the 2024 filing status
Fact.Description: The amount Form 8801 lines 11, 33 and 54 subtract from 28 percent of their base: $2,326 when /form8801PriorYearFilingStatusWasMarriedFilingSeparately is true, $4,652 when it is false. Incomplete when the 2024 status is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 11 by the rate rule for the stated 2024 filing status
Fact.Description: The All others branch of Form 8801 line 11 figured on /form8801Line10ExclusionItemsBaseOverTheExemption with the breakpoint and subtraction of the stated 2024 filing status: 26 percent at or below /form8801PriorYearAmtRateBreakpoint, otherwise 28 percent less /form8801PriorYearAmtRateSubtraction. Incomplete when the 2024 status is unanswered or line 10 is Incomplete. An arm of /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase.

Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 33 figured on /form8801Line32OrdinaryPortionOfTheBase with the breakpoint and subtraction of the stated 2024 filing status. Incomplete when the 2024 status is unanswered or line 32 is Incomplete. An arm of /form8801Line33TaxOnTheOrdinaryPortion.

Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 54 figured on /writableForm8801Line27PartThreeBase with the breakpoint and subtraction of the stated 2024 filing status. Incomplete when the 2024 status is unanswered or line 27 is unanswered. An arm of /form8801Line54TaxAtTheFlatAmtRates.

Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 20: "Enter your 2024 unallowed qualified electric vehicle credit (see instructions)." A DOCUMENTED ZERO for every return this dictionary supports. PART III REACHES THE CREDIT CHAIN. Line 11 is /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase, whose FIRST arm is /form8801Line55TaxOnExclusionItemsFromPartThree whenever Part III was worked, so Part III reaches line 13, line 15, line 18 and the minimum tax credit without the filer copying line 55 across by hand.

Fact.Description: Line 34 minus the nonnegative line 35, before the printed "If zero or less, enter -0-" is applied. The line 35 operand is floored at $0 so a malformed negative prior-year ordinary-income seed cannot inflate bracket room. NO PRINTED BOX MAPS IT.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 36, the room left in the 2024 zero percent bracket
Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 36 = line 34 minus line 35, floored at zero by the printed "If zero or less, enter -0-". PART III REACHES THE CREDIT CHAIN. Line 11 is /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase, whose FIRST arm is /form8801Line55TaxOnExclusionItemsFromPartThree whenever Part III was worked, so Part III reaches line 13, line 15, line 18 and the minimum tax credit without the filer copying line 55 across by hand.

Fact.Name: Form 8801 line 38, preferential income taxed at zero percent

PART III REACHES THE CREDIT CHAIN. Line 11 is /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase, whose FIRST arm is /form8801Line55TaxOnExclusionItemsFromPartThree whenever Part III was worked, so Part III reaches line 13, line 15, line 18 and the minimum tax credit without the filer copying line 55 across by hand.

Line 11 is /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase, whose FIRST arm is /form8801Line55TaxOnExclusionItemsFromPartThree whenever Part III was worked, so Part III reaches line 13, line 15, line 18 and the minimum tax credit without the filer copying line 55 across by hand.

Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 50 = line 32 plus line 47 plus line 48: the ordinary portion plus everything taxed at zero, fifteen, and twenty percent. Fact.Description: Form 8801 line 51 = line 27 minus line 50: the part of the exclusion items base that is unrecaptured section 1250 gain and is therefore taxed at 25 percent on line 52. Line 11 is /form8801Line11TentativeTaxOnTheExclusionItemsBase, whose FIRST arm is /form8801Line55TaxOnExclusionItemsFromPartThree whenever Part III was worked, so Part III reaches line 13, line 15, line 18 and the minimum tax credit without the filer copying line 55 across by hand.

THE ATTESTATION IS KEPT AS THE SECOND ARM, behind a real predicate: line 51 is Incomplete on the two printed skip paths into line 53, because /writableForm8801Line27PartThreeBase is unanswered there, and on those returns this fact is the filer's own entry and then $0, exactly what line 53 reads. Fact.Name: Form 3921 box 1, date option granted
Fact.Description: Form 3921: box 1, "Date option granted" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3921.pdf, page 1; employee instruction at lines 53-54). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 1 — Date the option was granted" (date), on every Form 3921 item; never required. Help text: The form's own employee instruction: box 1 "Shows the date the option to purchase the stock was granted to you." It is one end of the two holding periods the qualifying-disposition test turns on (two years from grant, one year from transfer); this dictionary does not run that test from these boxes, and a disposition is reported on its own Form 8949 row. Fact.Name: Form 3921 box 3, exercise price per share
Fact.Description: Form 3921: box 3, "Exercise price per share" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f3921.pdf, page 1; employee instruction at line 58). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 3 — Exercise price per share" (dollar amount), on every Form 3921 item; never required. Help text: The form's own employee instruction: box 3 "Shows the exercise price per share of stock." NOT ROUTED, and deliberately: Form 6251 line 2i is /writableAmtLine2iIncentiveStockOptions, the RETURN-LEVEL amount by which the AMT income on the exercise exceeds the regular-tax income, which the filer works out from boxes 3, 4 and 5 across every Form 3921 they hold. This dictionary does not compute it from these boxes and that fact is unchanged. Transcribed to the cent: a Dollar writable stores whole cents, so an exercise price the form quotes below a cent (for example $0.0125 or $4.2575) rounds to the nearest cent here and the sub-cent part is lost. The successor is a Rational or String transcription of the printed figure, typed by the Form 6251 line 2i computation that would consume it with boxes 4 and 5; until that computation exists the type stays Dollar. Validation: Dollar, Min $0, whole cents. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — Form 6251 line 2i stays /writableAmtLine2iIncentiveStockOptions, the RETURN-LEVEL adjustment the filer works out from this form among others.
